title: "patrinia yellow" for Clarinet and Computer
summary: An eleven-minute composition and live performance for clarinet and computer expressing the annual cycle of the yellow patrinia (ominaeshi) plant. The sound consists of the clarinet, parts of the clarinet recorded in real time, and computer processing of those recordings, in three sections: clarinet and computer together, a computer solo, and clarinet and computer again. It premiered in Korea in 2013 and received an Excellence Award in the Art Division of the 18th Japan Media Arts Festival (2014).

title: #MementoMori
summary: #MementoMori is a 2.35 x 1.45 m light box with a backlit print lit by LEDs, connected to a pre-programmed light-flashing device with 10 reactions. According to its signed text, it puts together 'the serialization of Lincoln' and a phrase taken from Facebook recalling a friend who disappeared in the 'War on drugs'. It was shown at the 13th Bienal de Artes Mediales in Santiago de Chile (2017).

title: (antiquated) Augmented Reality
summary: (antiquated) Augmented Reality is a live performance directed by Christine Marie (producer Nion McEvoy) in which an ensemble of dancers (Taylor Unwin, Sandra Ruiz, Melissa Ferrari) performs as giant stereoscopic shadows, up to about 30 feet tall, cast with a non-digital, pre-cinematic stereo imaging technique. The audience views the shadows through anaglyph 3D glasses, so that the figures appear to step off the screen and reach into the room. It was shown in the Films and Performances part of the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier programme in 2019.

title: 2.6g 329m/s (Bulletproof Skin)
summary: 2.6g 329m/s, also known as Bulletproof Skin, is a bio-art project in which in vitro human skin was reinforced with spider silk produced by genetically modified organisms (transgenic goats and silkworms) and then shot at with .22 calibre Long Rifle bullets; the title is the bullet weight and velocity a Type 1 bulletproof vest must stop. The skin stopped bullets fired at reduced speed but not at full speed. It was made with the Forensic Genomics Consortium Netherlands, Utah State University, Leiden University Medical Center and the Netherlands Forensic Institute.

title: 3FACE
media: Online / net art | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: An edition of 4,096 NFT artworks on the Ethereum blockchain, released through the platform Outland. Each 3FACE reads its owner's wallet and public transaction history, interprets it through a personality model of Nature, Nurture and Posture developed by Cheng, and renders a generative portrait; the owner can update the reading as the wallet accrues more history. MoMA and the Whitney Museum acquired editions in 2023.

title: 3SDC (Sunlight, Soil & Shit (De)Cycle)
artist: Oron Catts, Ionat Zurr & Steve Berrick
media: Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction | Network / data
summary: A working installation made of four linked parts: a compost-heated incubator growing mouse muscle cells as lab-grown meat, an alkaline hydrolysis unit that turns tissue and slaughterhouse refuse into fertiliser, hydroponic beds growing plants without soil, and a control room collecting sensor data from the other parts. It was first staged as a three-week durational experiment at PS Art Space, Fremantle, in February 2022, with public workshops, a symposium, dinner events, live streaming and a documentary. It received an Award of Distinction in Artificial Intelligence & Life Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: [help me know the truth]
media: Camera / computer vision | Screen / monitor | Projection
summary: [help me know the truth] is a networked software installation in which visitors take a selfie that is sent to tablets around the gallery. Using the reverse-correlation method from cognitive neuroscience, the software adds noise to the face and other visitors choose between two altered versions in response to prompts such as which face is more trustworthy or which is the terrorist. The face resulting from repeated choices is shown on a large projection.

title: [ir]reverent: Miracles on Demand
summary: [ir]reverent: Miracles on Demand is an installation built around a bio-incubator modelled on a Roman Catholic monstrance. A Eucharist host is placed in its oculus and inoculated with micro-droplets of the bacterium Serratia marcescens, which over about two days grows a blood-like red fluid on the wafer, reproducing the 'bleeding host' miracles recorded since antiquity.

title: A Performing by Flash, Afterimage, Velocity and Noise
summary: A multi-channel audiovisual installation with stereo and 5.1 surround sound, shown in the Korean Pavilion (History Has Failed Us, but No Matter) at the 58th Venice Biennale in 2019. It presents the performance of second-generation yeoseong gukgeuk male-role actor Lee Deung Woo together with four contemporary performers: electronic musician KIRARA, actor Yii Lee, performer and director Seo Ji Won, and drag king AZANGMAN. It is part of the artist's Yeoseong Gukgeuk Project (2008–).

title: A Tale of Two Seeds: Sound and Silence in Latin America's Andean Plain
summary: A sound installation built from field recordings of soils and plants in Colombia's Eastern Plains, recorded above and below ground, together with recordings of the electrical conductivity of soy and amaranth plants, which are sonified. FACT describes the recordings as contrasting soy monocultures with soy-amaranth polycultures, where amaranth grows despite herbicide use. Accompanying video works (On Vegetal Politics, Botánica Transgénica) and a blockchain application address the stock-market valuation and patenting of genetically modified plants; the work received the 2023 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica in Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: A Thousand Thoughts
summary: A Thousand Thoughts is a 'live documentary' portrait of the Kronos Quartet by Sam Green and Joe Bini, who are credited together with directing, writing and editing it. Green narrates live on stage while the Kronos Quartet performs the score, alongside archival footage, photos and interviews with the quartet and collaborators such as Philip Glass, Laurie Anderson, Terry Riley, Tanya Tagaq and Steve Reich. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier section in 2018 and toured to venues including the Wexner Center and the Barbican Hall, London.

title: Absence
summary: Absence is a 3D-animated short film (10 min per the artist, 12 min per the producer Autour de Minuit), in French with English subtitles. An old homeless man collapses alone in a square; passers-by avoid, ignore or help him, until journalists take an interest and he becomes the centre of an escalating media event. It received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Acconci Robot
summary: A robot in the form of a plain wooden crate that stays motionless while a visitor approaches, follows the visitor once they turn away, and stops when they look back. It refers to Vito Acconci's 1969 performance Following Piece; it was commissioned by Experimenta for its 5th International Biennale of Media Art (Speak to Me, 2012) and shown at ISEA2013 at the Powerhouse Museum, Sydney.

title: Acoustic Additive Synthesizer
summary: The Acoustic Additive Synthesizer (AAS) is a small computer-controlled pipe organ of seven pipes, each with a motorised piston that changes pitch continuously and a motorised air valve that changes volume; a Pure Data patch uses Fourier analysis to resynthesise sound with the pipes. Visitors speak or sing into a microphone on a stand and the instrument tries to repeat what it hears. The first version, with motorised bellows, was commissioned for the INSTALAKCJE 4 festival in 2015; a second version was built for the multimedia opera Aaron S at Warsaw Autumn 2016.

title: African Space Makers
summary: A 50-minute interactive 360-degree VR experience made in Nairobi, shown in Venice VR Expanded 2020. The viewer chooses a gender and the order in which to visit five creative spaces run by Nairobi collectives, and in each space chooses what to do and where to go next.

title: After Voices
summary: After Voices is an installation commissioned by Sherman Contemporary Art Foundation (SCAF), Sydney, as its Project 32 (2016, curated by Alia Swastika). Visitors walk through a procession of life-size 'ghost figures' without bodies, built from helmets, uniforms, mechanical clapping hands, musical instruments and motorcycle headlights, among rows of empty shoes, loudspeakers, flags, megaphones, drums and monitors, with kinetic movement and a layered soundscape. Video elements include a re-enactment of the 1 March 1949 Yogyakarta General Offensive; the work refers to the protests and upheaval after the 1998 fall of Suharto's New Order.

title: AI and the Art of Historical Reinterpretation – Filling Gender Bias Gaps
summary: An ongoing project that uses AI image generation to build a growing fictional archive of 'historical images' in which male figures in known historical photographs are replaced by female or nonbinary figures; the collection is spread across digital platforms so it can be scraped as training data for future AI models. In the exhibition installation, a selection of images related to technology is shown with a slide projector on a vintage projection screen.

title: AI War Cloud Database
media: Network / data | Online / net art | AI / generative
summary: AI War Cloud Database is an online interactive database and visualisation (aiwar.cloud) that catalogues AI systems used to make automated decisions in warfare and maps where the same types of tools appear in commercial products such as iris scanners, chatbots, robot vacuums and mapping tools, along with the companies and governments involved. Users explore the material through network graphs, a searchable table and interactive stories; the project describes itself as both an interactive database and a tangible interactive installation. It received the S+T+ARTS Prize 2025 Grand Prize – Artistic Exploration and was shown in the S+T+ARTS Prize exhibition at Ars Electronica Festival 2025 in Linz.

title: All That Perishes at the Edge of Land
summary: All That Perishes at the Edge of Land is a docu-fictional HD video by Hira Nabi set at the Gadani shipbreaking yards in Balochistan, Pakistan, in which a decommissioned container vessel, 'Ocean Master', is given a voice and converses with the migrant workers who dismantle it. It was developed through a residency at Vasl, Karachi, and commissioned by the Lahore Biennale Foundation, where it was shown looped at LB01 in 2018; a roughly 30-minute film version circulated at festivals from 2019.

title: AmaHubo
summary: AmaHubo is a 13-minute digital 4K video shown as a three-panel projection with sound, filmed on a wine farm in Tulbagh, Western Cape, that still has an old slave bell. It features black women on the farm; in its 2023–24 showing in 'Seers Seekers Soothsayers' at Zeitz MOCAA the artist is heard narrating a psalm while the gallery walls carry raised outlines of Cape landmarks such as Table Mountain.

title: An Unforeseen Situation
summary: An Unforeseen Situation is a video work by Bani Abidi relating to a series of state-run competitions organised by the Ministry of Sport in Punjab, Pakistan, in 2014, during which the country was reported to have broken several world records. Abidi tells her own version of such an event: a failed competition for the greatest mass singing of the national anthem, in which, according to a review in Open magazine, plastic chairs are piled up because nobody turned up. It was the title work of her solo exhibition at Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (n.b.k.), Berlin, 7 March – 30 April 2017.

title: Angles Mirror
media: Robotics / kinetics | Camera / computer vision | Material / sculpture
summary: Angles Mirror is a wall-mounted triangular steel sculpture holding 465 yellow plastic spokes, each turned by a motor and driven by a video camera, control electronics and custom software. When a viewer stands in front of it, the spokes rotate to angles that trace the contours and movement of the viewer's figure rather than light and dark; when the viewer moves away, the surface runs through predefined images and transitions. It was shown in Rozin's solo exhibition Angles at bitforms gallery, New York, in 2013 and received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: Anthem
summary: Anthem is an installation of four suspended devices modelled on tree tumours (burls), 3D-printed and fitted with speakers, microphones and sound processors. It responds in real time to visitors' vocalisations with machine-generated animal-like calls. It was first shown at the centre of Santillán's exhibition ¿Qué se siente ser tierra? at the Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito (2025–2026) and again at the 2026 Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale.

title: Antraal
summary: Antraal is an artificial intelligence program by Sahej Rahal presented on cathode-ray television monitors and as a video projection, shown with his sculptures Other limbs (2019) in ACCA's exhibition Feedback Loops (Melbourne, 7 December 2019 – 22 March 2020). What the visitor sees is not edited video but the program's environments, in which characters devised by the artist move according to algorithmic instructions. ACCA's label gives the title as roughly meaning 'interstice', a space between, in Sanskrit.

title: Anxious Body
summary: Anxious Body is a 5'47 2D digital animated short without dialogue, commissioned by Towada Art Center and produced by Miyu Productions and New Deer (2021), with sound by Yuka C. Honda. It shows fingers, cellophane tape and a dispenser, a mechanical pencil, tennis racket strings, a sponge and a snake-like creature touching, pulling and pressing against one another. It received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Any Ever
summary: Any Ever is a series of seven movies by Ryan Trecartin, made in collaboration with Lizzie Fitch and largely filmed over two years in a house in Miami that served as both their home and the set. In 2011 it was shown at MoMA PS1 and MOCA Miami at the same time, after opening at The Power Plant in Toronto. At PS1 the movies played inside 'sculptural theaters' made with Fitch, which visitors sit in to watch; the movies are also online.

title: APHASIA
summary: APHASIA is a video installation of four vertical screens side by side, each showing a performance by one of four women from different periods of Taiwanese history, all played by the artist. According to the artist the characters are a woman speaking Shanghai dialect, a woman in a pink kimono from the Japanese period, a Hakka woman and a woman of the 1980s, based on her hometown Hsinchu. It was shown at the SVA gallery in New York in 2014 and at Reed College, Portland, in 2015, and was a Jury Selection in the 18th Japan Media Arts Festival Art Division.

title: Ausente
media: Camera / computer vision | AI / generative | Projection
summary: An interactive installation (Dyscrimina / Ausente) presented at the 44th International Symposium of Contemporary Art of Baie-Saint-Paul: a surveillance-style projection shows visitors in real time, and people are erased from the frame. Across four stations using AI and computer vision, the public collectively teaches the machine which characteristics to recognize; those outside the resulting vocabulary are designated « non-choisi.e » and progressively removed from the image.

title: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β
summary: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β is a permanent café in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, run by Ory Lab, where people who have difficulty going out because of illness, disability, caregiving or distance work as “pilots”, remotely operating the avatar robots OriHime and OriHime-D from home or hospital through the robots' cameras, microphones and speakers, in some cases by eye-gaze input. Visitors are seated, order, are served drinks and talk with the pilots through the robots; the project also matches pilots with employers through Ory Lab's Avatar Guild staffing agency. It received the Golden Nica in Digital Communities at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Awakening
summary: A projection mapping work shown on the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), made by Tororo.aoi (Asher Yeo) as part of the festival's third Projection Mapping Masterclass, led by the Malaysian collective Filamen. According to the festival, it takes Singapore's island and port history as its subject, starting from a metaphorical dive into a shipwreck.

title: Azibuye – The Occupation
summary: Azibuye – The Occupation is a 360-degree virtual reality documentary following Masello Motana, a performance artist, and Evan Abrahamse, an activist and former Umkhonto we Sizwe member, who occupy a mansion in an affluent part of Johannesburg that has stood empty and decaying for about 20 years, as an act about land ownership. The viewer is placed inside the house with them; the film includes a recorded phone interview with the house's owner. Produced by Electric South, it premiered in the New Frontier section of the Sundance Film Festival in 2020.

title: Añoranzas (Yira Yira)
summary: Añoranzas (Yira Yira) is an installation with 16mm colour film made by recycling celluloid combs, screened with a 16mm film projector. It refers to Argentine film pioneer Federico Valle, whose surviving films, after a 1926 fire, were sold to a comb factory that used the celluloid as raw material. The work was realised with a 2023 CIFO-Ars Electronica Award and shown at the LENTOS Kunstmuseum during Ars Electronica Festival 2023.

title: Baitul Ma'mur: House of Angels
summary: A bio-art project by Sarah Khan and Joe Davis that encodes the Arabic phrase "Subhan Allah" multiple times into synthesized DNA molecules, using a coding scheme modelled on the repeating geometries of Islamic art; according to the artists, a 1mm layer of this DNA on the head of a straight pin holds 2.417 quintillion repetitions ("angels"). The work is presented with a glass and aluminum "Baitul Ma'mur" structure with electronics, project graphics and a short documentary film. It received an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2021, Artificial Intelligence & Life Art category.

title: Balance From Within
summary: Balance From Within is a 170-year-old sofa that balances on one of its four legs. A computer-controlled mechanism inside it, based on the reaction wheel used in satellites, keeps correcting its position, and its motors make humming and creaking sounds. A push from a visitor or another outside force can knock it over; its main parts are held together with magnets so that it can be put back together. It received an Award of Distinction for Interactive Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

title: Batil-Kobitaoli (Poems Declined)
summary: Batil-Kobitaoli (Poems Declined) is a multi-media installation commissioned for the second Dhaka Art Summit (2014), built from unpublished and rejected poems that the artist collected from aspiring poets and publishers in Dhaka. It includes a unique, unedited book of 1,800 declined poems, painted works made from the correction marks on the manuscripts, and doodled self-corrections from the manuscripts projected onto the gallery ceiling as shadow drawings. The work was shown again in Sen's survey mOTHERTONGUE at the Australian Centre for Contemporary Art, Melbourne, in 2023.

title: Behind Shirley
media: Screen / monitor | VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture
summary: An installation made in 2020 consisting of a video-essay, two 3D-printed busts and an augmented reality application. It addresses the 'Shirley cards' used to calibrate skin tones in colour photography and the failure of current facial recognition software to register darker skin. It was shown at the 5th Istanbul Design Biennial (2020) and in the exhibition Digital Shadows at OBA Oosterdok, Amsterdam (until 26 Feb 2023), and received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Behind the Sun
summary: Behind the Sun is a 10-minute single-channel video commissioned by Beirut Art Center in 2013. It combines amateur VHS footage, filmed in 1991 by Adil Al Yousifi, of the Kuwaiti oil fields set ablaze during the retreat of invading forces after the first Gulf War with audio monologues from Islamic television programmes of the same period, taken from the Kuwait Television archives. It was shown in the Berlinale Forum Expanded in 2014.

title: Believe me
summary: A web-based work commissioned by the Whitney Museum for artport, made in collaboration with Leander Herzog. In the browser, the visitor sees a series of images (political scenes, interface elements, internet folklore, among them the American flag) overlaid with the visual effect of a cracked, glitching screen; clicking shifts the fractured image and refreshing the page loads a new one. The title takes the two words Donald Trump used most often, according to a 2017 analysis by sociolinguist Jennifer Sclafani for CNN.

title: Bemol
summary: An installation of video, photography and sound composition shown at Centro Cultural Recoleta for the 17th Bienal de Artes Mediales de Santiago (2025). It is built from audio recordings, photographs and video the artist made of her home and its surroundings in Santiago's Barrio Yungay after resettling there in 2024, assembled as what she calls an 'anti-archive'; two sound-visual concerts accompanied it.

title: Best of Luck with the Wall
summary: Best of Luck with the Wall is a short film that travels the full length of the US-Mexico border, stitched together from about 200,000 satellite images downloaded by script using the coordinates of the boundary line and the existing border fence. It was edited with Laura Poitras and Field of Vision, with an original score by Jace Clayton (DJ /rupture), and published by The Intercept in October 2016.

title: Between the Waves
summary: Between the Waves is a five-channel video installation with multi-channel sound (total running time 86 minutes) in which performers wearing unicorn-like horns and costumes made from refuse appear on a polluted shore, in a mangrove forest, under water and on a landfill, alongside animation and a burning moon. Channel 1 is a longer film that forms the backbone of the installation; the channel Landfill Dance, made with dancers of the Hrishikesh Pawar Contemporary Dance Company and Linda Borini, serves as an epilogue. It was commissioned by Carolyn Christov-Bakargiev and premiered at dOCUMENTA (13) in Kassel in 2012.

title: biko.fanon
summary: biko.fanon is an installation of receipt printers and a micro-controller that print texts from the writings of Steve Biko and Frantz Fanon, with the printers mounted on the gallery wall. It was listed as Biko.Fanon, 2018 in Dennis's solo exhibition Options at Goodman Gallery, Cape Town (2019), and was shown again in the survey Understudies at Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2024–25). Goodman Gallery describes a later work, biko.nomzamo, as extending the artist's 'Biko dialogues' series (2018-ongoing).

title: Birth (of a Nation)
summary: Birth (of a Nation) is a seven-channel video installation with soundscape and computer terminal (about one hour) by Centro Audiovisual Max Stahl Timor-Leste (CAMSTL), commissioned for the Singapore Biennale 2019. It presents material drawn from the CAMSTL archive, founded in 2003 and holding more than 6,000 hours of audiovisual material on Timor-Leste, through which, according to the Singapore Art Museum, visitors encounter the country's history and culture and the Timorese struggle for democracy and nationhood. The archive's independence-struggle collection, 'On the Birth of a Nation: Turning Points', was inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

title: Black Friday
summary: Black Friday is a 16:36-minute digital video with sound, projected vertically, shot largely in an unopened shopping mall in Doha; an unseen narrator speaks over images of marble halls, shuttered shops, blurred faces and a figure lying on the mall floor. At the Whitney Museum (26 July–31 October 2016) the projection hung above The Litany, a heap of old electronic screens playing short glitchy loops, in a free-access ground-floor gallery.

title: Blade Runner—Autoencoded
summary: Blade Runner—Autoencoded is a film made by training an autoencoder, a type of generative neural network, on every frame of Ridley Scott's Blade Runner (1982) and then having it reconstruct each frame in order. The reconstructed frames are resequenced into a version of the film that stays close to the original in static scenes and becomes hard to recognise in scenes with much movement. It was made as the artist's MSci dissertation project in Creative Computing at Goldsmiths, University of London.

title: Blank Project #3 Cosmos
summary: The third work in Mihara's Blank Project, begun after the 11 March 2011 Tohoku earthquake, built from moss, soil and electricity (the artist's site also lists mirror, spectral film and motor). In the Seoul version a moss-covered marble rolls around the exhibition hall; Mihara researched Korean moss on site and compared it with Japanese moss. At SeMA Biennale Mediacity Seoul 2016 it was shown at three museum branches on different dates.

title: Broken Spectre
summary: Broken Spectre (2022) is a feature-length immersive video installation (about 70–74 minutes) on deforestation and environmental crime along the Trans-Amazonian Highway in the Brazilian Amazon, made with cinematographer Trevor Tweeten and composer Ben Frost. It alternates footage from an aerial multispectral camera flown from a helicopter, ultraviolet macro time-lapse of the forest floor, and black-and-white infrared 35mm film of ranchers, gold miners and Indigenous communities, including a speech to camera by Yanomami woman Adneia. Visitors watch it in a gallery with a spatialised soundtrack; it received the 2023 S+T+ARTS Grand Prize – Innovative Collaboration.

title: Build Up the House II
summary: Build Up the House II is an animated video shown on more than 92 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight throughout March 2025 as part of Midnight Moment, presented with ART on THE MART. Silhouettes of dancers leap, spin and vogue across colored patterns that reference the artist's East African heritage and textiles, as an homage to house music and its queer and POC roots. It follows Build Up the House, a 2024 projection on the facade of THE MART in Chicago marking the 40th anniversary of house music; a public DJ dance party accompanied the Times Square presentation on 14 March 2025.

title: but that is not the important part of the story
summary: An installation made for the 12th Biennale de Lyon (2013) and shown at the Musée d'art contemporain de Lyon; according to the Biennale guide it was first created as a performance in South Africa before being sent to Lyon. Wikipedia describes it as made up of wooden beams draped in white fabric, electrical cables, screens, rear-view mirrors, a small fan and sound recordings. It was shown again in 2014 in Ruffneck Constructivists, curated by Kara Walker, at the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia.

title: Café Kuba
summary: A cinematic installation (film, about 27 minutes, in French and Lingala, with 3D sound) built around a mobile street coffee cart in Kinshasa that Shongo converted into a recording device. Filmed after the M23 capture of Goma and Bukavu in early 2025, it follows the cart and a coffee vendor through the city's streets and conversations, with fictional elements such as masked figures holding electronic waste and licence plates; it won the State of the ART(ist) prize at Ars Electronica 2025.

title: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Power and Technology, 1500-2025
summary: A diagram more than 24 metres long and 3 metres high, made as a diptych of hundreds of hand-drawn illustrations and short texts, that maps communication, computation, classification and control from 1500 to the present. Time runs vertically and systems run horizontally, so visitors can follow a theme, a period or a set of ideas. Two handmade books are shown with it, and visitors are invited to annotate them in pencil.

title: Cangjie's Poetry
media: AI / generative | Camera / computer vision | Projection
summary: An installation in which an AI system named Cangjie, a neural network trained on the constructions of over 9,000 Chinese characters, watches its surroundings through a camera and turns the live feed into new symbols built from Chinese strokes, shown as a moving pixelated landscape on a first projection. A second projection shows descriptive sentences the system generates about the scene, rendered as flowing ink 'poetry' assembled with fragments of the captured imagery. Visitors meet both projections changing in real time with what the camera sees.

title: Carbon Black
summary: Carbon Black (Noir de carbone) is a series of 15 photographic prints of the sky made in collaboration with climate modellers Rita van Dingenen and Jean-Philippe Putaud (Joint Research Centre, European Commission). From Fair Isle, the scientists traced the black carbon particles in the air back to their emission point in Folkestone harbour; Tondeur then travelled the 837-mile route by foot, boat and car, photographing the sky each day and filtering particles through a breathing mask. The particles were extracted and turned into ink, with which each photograph is printed; the exhibition also shows maps, masks and the extracted particles.

title: catástrofe orquestra #1 (Ato I)
summary: An installation made for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo (2025): 11 suspended panels of recycled matchbox fragments on thin wooden slats, among which 64 motor-driven rope pendulums carrying pieces of coal strike leather drums. The coal shatters on impact; the sounds are picked up by microphones and amplified into a soundscape with noises and voices, and the debris accumulates on the floor. The work later travelled with the Bienal's itinerant exhibitions, including to the Pinacoteca do Ceará and the Centro Cultural La Moneda in Santiago.

title: CENTO
media: VR / AR / XR | Online / net art | Screen / monitor
summary: CENTO is an augmented-reality creature, geolocated above the eighth-floor terrace of the Whitney Museum of American Art, together with a video that tours the creature's imagined habitat (nest, refueling chamber, and the space where it metabolizes fuel and takes flight). Using the free 4th Wall app, on site or from anywhere, viewers choose one of twelve feathers, each with a function such as communication, navigation or energy conversion, and add it to the creature's body, which is updated over time. It is a Whitney artport commission; the title refers to a poem made of lines taken from other poets' works.

title: Chijikinkutsu
summary: A sound installation made of water, sewing needles, glass tumblers and coils of copper wire. Magnetized needles float on the water in the tumblers and align north-south with the earth's magnetic field; when current is switched to a coil on the outside of a tumbler, the temporary magnetic field draws the needle against the glass, producing a faint sound, with the switching sequenced by MIDI from an iPad app through custom controllers. The title combines "chijiki" (geomagnetism) and "suikinkutsu", an Edo-period sound device for Japanese gardens; the work received the Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2015.

title: CHIMERIA
media: Performance / body | VR / AR / XR | Camera / computer vision
summary: CHIMERIA is a project, performance and installation in which head-mounted displays move a participant's vision to other parts of the body, such as the toes, so that the feet act as the head. Volunteers recruited through a publicly circulated phone number lived together in a Tokyo residence, adapting to an environment built for upright bodies with tube-fed liquid food, wire-driven prosthetics and a toilet used kneeling. Outsiders could visit the space, but only by imitating the environment and becoming part of it.

title: Chosho Hakkei in Rittor Base - HPL ver
summary: A five-track, roughly 42-minute 3D audio album for headphone listening, made with the HPL binaural process developed with engineer Jiro Kubo (ACOUSTIC FIELD). It reconstructs evala's 2019 sound installations 'Chosho Hakkei' in the Nakazu Banshou-en daimyo garden in Marugame, Kagawa, placed on a bridge, on a small island and in the oldest extant tea house there, first restaged as a 3D sound piece at Rittor Base. Listeners follow, on headphones, a route through the garden's recorded and composed sounds.

title: Chotlung: traversing spirits, redemptive songs
summary: A single-channel video (8:50 minutes) shown with a textile installation of pieces handwoven by the artist, co-commissioned by Colomboscope and Ghost 2568 and exhibited at Colomboscope: Rhythm Alliances in Colombo. The video shows looms and Yakthung rituals at Mukkumlung sacred mountain and the Imbiri Yangthangwa (Tamor river) region of eastern Nepal, alongside protests against hydropower dams and a proposed cable car; the textiles have also been carried in demonstrations.

title: Chuly? Chuly
summary: An XR video game and live motion-capture performance (Ukrainian title Чули? Чули, 'Have you heard? We've heard' / 'Have you felt it? We've felt it'), first developed as a demo in Deep Space 8K at the Ars Electronica Center. In the first act a player crosses a game world guided by an AI-processed narration of a woman's story of seeing giants; in the second a dancer in an inertial motion-capture suit, whose calibration drifts, enters, and player and dancer exchange suit parts and controller, so the player becomes a non-player character and the dancer controls the camera. It received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: Cihuapapalutzin
media: Robotics / kinetics | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: A swarm of 104 robotic monarch butterflies made from recycled aluminium beer and soft-drink cans, with electronics, mechanics and software. It was commissioned by the Toronto Biennial of Art and shown at 259 Lake Shore Blvd East in 2019. The butterflies are programmed to respond to seismic frequencies and are split into two groups of 52, which refers to a Mesoamerican ceremony that links the 365-day and 260-day calendars.

title: Circles of Rhythm and Rains
summary: Circles of Rhythm and Rains (also given as Circle of Rhythms / Circle of Rhythms & Rains) is a kinetic sound installation shown at the Rio Complex for Colomboscope 2026, co-commissioned with 421 Arts Campus. Traditional Tamil drums used in Koothu (thavil, mathalam, udukkai, parai, mirudhangam), handcrafted with artisan Vadivel Aananthashankar from reclaimed wood and repurposed materials, are arranged in a circle and struck by automated tappers driven by Arduino and motors, built with DreamSpace Academy/lab. Visitors meet programmed, pulsating beat cycles played without a human drummer.

title: Codex Virtualis_Genesis
summary: An AI-art-science project that generates an open-ended taxonomic collection of speculative life forms by training generative networks on microscopy footage of bacteria and archaea combined with cellular-automata models. The installation, distributed across three projections, shows the process from the simplest organisms through 'virtual genesis' to a final rendering with an AI-generated taxonomic name. It was made during the SETI x AI residency (SETI Institute and Ars Electronica Futurelab, European ARTificial Intelligence Lab) in 2021 and received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: Coin Laundry
summary: Coin Laundry is an installation by the pseudonymous artist XCOPY, presented on the Nguyen Wahed stand in the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach in December 2025 and staged as a laundromat. According to the gallery, participants enter an ephemeral network through fungible tokens inscribed in code, in a collective performance planned to last a decade; the work was presented in partnership with Shape.

title: Collective Body
media: VR / AR / XR | Performance / body | Sound
summary: Collective Body is a 19-minute multi-user virtual reality dance experience set in a New Mexican storm, in which participants are guided through stages: beginning alone, discovering the unfamiliar, first encounters and moving together. An algorithmic system analyses each participant's movement and assigns one of sixteen avatars, each represented as a natural element with its own musical theme; participants then meet one other person and finally the whole group. It runs on Meta Quest 3 headsets with almost full-body tracking and no other wearables; it was shown at Venice Immersive 2025 and at Lincoln Center.

title: Columbos
summary: A nine-minute stop-motion animated film by the Japanese duo KAWAI+OKAMURA (Hiroki Okamura and Takumi Kawai) in which a puppet of the TV detective Columbo appears at a homicide scene with the corpse of an actress dressed in red and a man with a gunshot wound. The catalogue describes it as a meta-mystery told through a montage of time and space and of fantasy and reality. It premiered at IFFR 2013 and received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation / Film / VFX at Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

title: Community of Parting
summary: Community of Parting is a 72-minute film presented as a double-channel video installation in the Korean Pavilion of the 58th Venice Biennale (2019). It invokes the Korean shamanic myth of the abandoned princess Bari and combines shamanic ritual performances and chants by shaman Koh Sunahn of Jeju Island, nature and cityscapes, archival material, aerial imagery, poetry, voiceover and soundscapes. It was filmed in locations including Jeju Island, the DMZ, South Korea, North Korea, Kazakhstan, Japan, China, the United States and Germany, with narratives by South Korean, North Korean and diasporic women.

title: Compose
summary: Yuko Mohri's exhibition for the Japan Pavilion at the 60th Venice Biennale (20 April to 24 November 2024), curated by Sook-Kyung Lee, made of two site-specific installations built mostly from materials found locally. In Moré Moré (Leaky), the artist creates water leaks in the pavilion and catches them with household goods, with pumps circulating the water through a large kinetic sculpture; rain can enter through the open ceiling. In Decomposition, electrodes in local fruit turn their changing moisture into signals that modulate drone sounds and lights as the fruit ripens and decays, after which it goes to compost.

title: Conspiracy: Conjoining the Virtual
media: VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture | Performance / body
summary: A participatory sculpture in which five people, each wearing a VR headset, are joined to one armature and play a game together in virtual space while the structure constrains their movement to side-to-side steps. Bellows between the headsets compress as participants move, so that the sculpture appears to breathe. The artist's site lists the work as 'Conspire' (2018): VR headsets, kinetic armature and an audio coach.

title: Convergence
summary: Convergence is a 35-minute piece for string ensemble and AI system, made with Ensemble Resonanz, that exists as a staged version (premiered in Bonn, October 2020; revised in Dresden, 2023) and a digital-only streamed version (premiered February 2021, commissioned by Eclat Festival). Deep-learning models (auto-encoders and GANs, with audio programming by IRCAM researchers) learn features of the musicians' faces, bodies and voices, and the performers, guided by a computer voice, interact with the generated counterparts of themselves. It won the 2021 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary
summary: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary is an ensemble of three interactive installations (a coffee vending machine, a photocopier and a microwave) fitted with sensors, custom software and generative AI so that they converse with visitors. Visitors have to persuade the coffee machine to brew them a coffee, draw doodles that the photocopier turns into rendered prints they can take home, and use the microwave to give a voice to objects placed inside it. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art+ at Prix Ars Electronica 2024 and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2024; the coffee machine and microwave were developed during a residency at iii (instrument inventors initiative).

title: Corpus Nil
summary: Corpus Nil is a 20-25 minute performance for one human performer and artificial-intelligence algorithms. In a dark space, Donnarumma, partly naked and painted black, performs a slow choreography while biosensors (chip microphones for muscle sounds and EMG electrodes) send data to software that learns his movement and chooses on its own how to generate multichannel sound and light, which in turn affects his movement. It premiered on 6 February 2016 at ZKM Karlsruhe and received an Award of Distinction in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2017.

title: Crossings
summary: Crossings is a three-channel video installation (6 minutes 20 seconds per Galleria Continua) about sub-Saharan migrants who leave their home countries hoping to reach Europe, and about their passage through Morocco. Told from the migrants' point of view, it combines voice-over testimonies, still portraits and reconstructed video landscapes to recreate the sensations of the journey. It was shown at the 5th Marrakech Biennale in 2014, at the Ecole supérieure des arts visuels (ESAV), with which it was produced.

title: Crystal Sounds of a Synchrotron
summary: A 38-minute surround-sound (5.1) work composed from frequencies generated by the electron storage ring of Diamond Light Source, the UK's synchrotron, mostly the sounds of electron injections into the accelerator, combined with binaural recordings made in its experimental hall, storage ring and beamlines. It was commissioned and published on DVD by Diamond Light Source and is designed both for concentrated listening and for installation, where listeners can enter at any point. It received the Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2012.

title: Dancer from the Peninsula
media: Screen / monitor | Performance / body | Material / sculpture
summary: Dancer from the Peninsula is a multi-channel video installation made for the Korean Pavilion of the 58th Venice Biennale (History Has Failed Us, but No Matter, 2019). It traces the dancer Choi Seung-hee (1911–1969) through her fragmented archive, focusing on the period after 1941 and her aim to create a modern East Asian dance, using found footage and images from her archives. The presentation in Venice also included a large sculptural structure and a small garden installed behind the pavilion.

title: Dari Pulau Ke Pulau (From One Island to Another)
summary: A projection mapping work shown on the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), made by HAFI (Hafizah Jainal) as part of the festival's third Projection Mapping Masterclass, led by the Malaysian collective Filamen. Using illustration and moving images, it traces the routes of the artist's maternal and paternal grandparents from Alor Gajah, Melaka, and Pacitan, East Java, to Singapore.

title: Das avós
summary: Das avós is a video installation commissioned for the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019), Rosana Paulino's first work in video. In a dark room, looping projections show short performances in which a young woman (performer Charlene Bicalho) comes into caring contact with images of Black women from colonial and 19th-century Brazil; brief flashes of images of enslaved people also appear.

title: Datum Point
media: Screen / monitor | Material / sculpture | Text / print
summary: A 6'41'' stop-motion clay animation based on the poem Suijun genten (Datum Point) by Yoshiro Ishihara (1915–77). Waves of white clay rise and swell, and the characters of the poem appear in them one at a time before being swallowed again; the artist shot it by hand over about a year, with music by Shun Owada. It screened in competition at Animafest Zagreb and Annecy in 2016.

title: Dead Drops
summary: Dead Drops is an anonymous, offline, peer-to-peer file-sharing network in public space: USB flash drives are cemented into walls, buildings and curbs, each installed empty except for a readme.txt file. Anyone can plug a laptop into a drop to leave or copy files, and anyone may install a new drop and submit its location to the project's database. Bartholl installed the first five in New York in October 2010 during an Eyebeam residency; the project was shown in MoMA's Talk to Me (2011) and has since spread to many countries.

title: Diary of a Madman
summary: A multi-video installation of fifteen videos made during a three-month residency at the New Museum, New York, in partnership with K11 Art Foundation, and shown in the museum's Lobby Gallery from October 2016 to January 2017. The diary-like vignettes, played on screens hung at varying heights, include footage from early-morning walks in New York, a trip to Staten Island Bay and a visit to an abandoned psychiatric hospital on Long Island; videos with dialogue carry Mandarin and English subtitles. The title is taken from Lu Xun's 1918 short story.

title: Different Shades of Water
summary: A series of five digital paintings made in Microsoft Word and issued as NFTs, restaging David Hockney's Portrait of an Artist (Pool with Two Figures) (1972) with a Black man as the poolside bather under different daylight and water colours. The works were shown at 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair at Somerset House, London, in October 2021 and auctioned online by Christie's, the first NFT by a contemporary African artist offered by Christie's in Europe.

title: Difficult Love
summary: Difficult Love is a 48-minute documentary, commissioned by the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) and co-directed by Zanele Muholi and Peter Goldsmid, about Muholi's life and work and the lives of Black lesbians in South Africa. It is built from interviews with Muholi, their family, partner and friends, and with people who appear in Muholi's photographs, who speak about their lives, relationships and experiences of violence. It was shot in 2010.

title: Dispatch
summary: Dispatch is a four-episode animated virtual-reality miniseries written and directed by Edward Robles at the studio Here Be Dragons, made in Unity with Oculus as financing partner, for the Oculus Rift and Gear VR. The viewer follows Ted, a small-town police dispatcher voiced by Martin Starr, through an all-night crime spree; the scenes on the other end of his calls are shown as sparse wireframe/vector graphics while most of the story is carried by voices and sound. The first episode debuted at the 2017 Venice International Film Festival and the last at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival (New Frontier).

title: Displuvium
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Network / data
summary: An installation in the form of a water-filled pool on the floor (weathering steel, black aluminium, distilled water), in which tiny underwater 3D-printed nozzles generate drops so the visitor sees 'rain' falling on the water surface. Two wall screens show a map of twelve historical rainfall events, some natural and some caused by human intervention such as cloud seeding; when controlled events are shown, the drops form recognisable patterns. Made with designer Renaud Defrancesco; shown in the 'Swiss Media Art' exhibition (!Mediengruppe Bitnik, Fragmentin, Lauren Huret) at H3K, Basel, and later in stone and circular editions.

title: Do Electric Sheep Dream 1, 2
artist: Tak Young Hwan and Lee Kyung Nam
summary: Two single-channel videos (part 1, 2 min with sound; part 2, 1 min 30 sec), digital compositions of images and text that look like a commercial advertisement or a juxtaposition of informational sign images, about human life in a near future as artificial intelligence permeates daily life. Commissioned by the 10th Seoul Mediacity Biennale (Eu Zên, Seoul Museum of Art, 2018); part 1 was also shown on the Seoullo Media Canvas building screen.

title: Dobra do tempo infinito (Fold of Infinite Time)
artist: Glicéria Tupinambá, Atã Tupinambá Group & Tupinambá Community of Serra do Padeiro
summary: Dobra do tempo infinito is a video installation shown in the Hãhãwpuá Pavilion (Brazil) at the 60th Venice Biennale, combining video with seeds, leaves, soil, fishing nets, jereré and samburá. The video records workshops Glicéria Tupinambá organised in the communities of Serra do Padeiro and Olivença (Bahia), in which masters made canoes, fishing nets and net-weaving needles and went fishing with trawls and tarrafas; the footage was shot by young people of the Atã Tupinambá Group with Augusto Santos (Method_av). The venue text links the stitches of fishing nets to the weaving of traditional Tupinambá clothing.

title: Dominus Trémulo
summary: Dominus Trémulo is a 6-minute digital short film in black and white and colour directed by Raúl Miranda (performance by Jorge Santos, music by Sebastián Jatz), in which a man begins his morning ritual and is interrupted by a tremor, real or imagined. The work refers to the 1647 Santiago earthquake and the colonial legend of the Señor de Mayo, and to the ruins of the Convento do Carmo in Lisbon left by the 1755 earthquake. In the installation the film is projected in a loop onto a floating paper screen that vibrates from a sub-bass speaker mounted behind it, driven by music based on Purcell's 'Dido's Lament'.

title: Double Poser
summary: Double Poser is a 38-minute auto-played game made with the Unity game engine (4k, colour, stereo sound), commissioned by the Hayward Gallery, London, and Art Sonje Center, Seoul, and shown in the Hayward's HENI Project Space from 1 December 2023 to 7 January 2024. Reinterpreting components of Kim's Cutter III (2023), it takes the Hayward's brutalist architecture as a starting point and combines computer-generated imagery, video game aesthetics and skateboarding culture. Visitors watch it as a video in the gallery.

title: Down with Wrestlers with Systems and Mental Nonadapters!
media: Robotics / kinetics | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: An interactive installation in which a visitor walks on a treadmill that sets in motion many small figures built into a 'social mechanism' of conveyor belts. Speaking the absurdist manifesto 'DA-DA' into a microphone sends a low-frequency pulse through a subwoofer that shakes hundreds of figures in a cellular structure above, so that some fall out of it. A miniature video camera on one conveyor shows on a monitor the inside of a black cube containing biomorphic sculptures; the installation measures 500 x 500 x 500 cm and was made with the Robotics Laboratory of the Moscow Polytechnic Museum.

title: Dreams Have No Titles
summary: Sedira's installation for the French Pavilion at the 59th Venice Biennale (2022): a series of interlocking film sets, including a re-creation of her London living room, a shelf of film reels referencing the Cinémathèque Algérienne, a ballroom bar and a cinema room, combined with a film of re-enactments and 'makings of' scenes. It draws on Algerian, French and Italian militant cinema of the 1960s and 1970s, including The Battle of Algiers and the rediscovered Les Mains libres. Visitors walk through the sets, watch the film and at times meet two performers dancing the tango.

title: Drifting Bodies
summary: A four-channel video installation (colour, sound, 10 min 30 sec, with curtains and mattress) that pairs a silent projection of the Jewel Rain Vortex indoor waterfall at Singapore's Changi Airport with three channels of footage and spatialised sound from Thailand's Vajiralongkorn Dam Reservoir, where displaced Karen families live on floating rafts; the two sites are linked by a shared hydroelectric power grid. Visitors walk through the waterfall projection screens to reach the reservoir footage. It was first shown at Storefront for Art and Architecture, New York (2025), and at Singapore Biennale 2025 alongside the sound work The Humming of the Power Grid and a fundraising Water Campaign for the reservoir community.

title: Dust Blooms: A Research Narrative in Artistic Ecology
media: Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction | Text / print
summary: Dust Blooms examines how well urban flowers filter airborne dust, in three parts. Dust was collected from seven wild roadside plant species on heavily trafficked Berlin streets and analysed under light microscopes; an exhibition laboratory with microscopes, slides, protocols and maps lets visitors look at the dust-covered petals themselves, next to a raised bed of the same species and photographs. It also includes seven botanical engravings printed with the collected street dust and shell gold, and dandelion-based sculptural prototypes made from consumer materials, with Arduino dust sensors that measure atmospheric dust levels.

title: E.m-bed.de/d, Datamosh, Augmented Real
media: Online / net art | Screen / monitor | VR / AR / XR
summary: E.m-bed.de/d is an interactive HTML5 music video by the rapper and artist Yung Jake. It opens a string of pop-up browser windows, each showing a different part of the same video, together with rising YouTube view counts and 'endorsements' from other accounts and sites. In Datamosh, the pixels that make up his image are digitally eroded while he raps about datamoshing. The 2013 Sundance Film Festival New Frontier listing describes him streaming into screenings, Skype-bombing DJ sets and appearing in augmented-reality music videos.

title: Ebb and Flow (A Onda Traz, o Vento Leva)
summary: Ebb and Flow is a 28-minute film produced by the Han Nefkens Foundation as part of a project of the ArtAids foundation, and shown at MACBA, Barcelona, 31 May to 4 June 2012. It follows Rodrigo, a young deaf man in Recife, northeast Brazil, who installs car stereos in a small dealership; a fixed camera stays close to his daily routine and his exchanges with others. Rodrigo is a fictional persona (played by Márcio Campelo Santana) and parts of the plot were scripted by Mascaro.

title: Electrical Walks
summary: Visitors borrow custom wireless headphones with built-in induction coils and a map of a city district on which the artist has marked routes and strong electromagnetic fields. Walking alone, in a group or on a guided tour, they hear the hums, pulses and drones of shop security gates, ATMs, trams, Wi-Fi, lighting and other infrastructure that normally cannot be heard. The series has run in cities worldwide since 2004, with walk no. 100 announced for Budapest in October 2026.

title: EMPEROR
summary: EMPEROR is a 40-minute single-user interactive VR narrative, produced by Atlas V with Reynard Films and France Télévisions, set inside the mind of a father with aphasia, drawn as a hand-drawn monochrome landscape. The user takes the father's point of view alongside his daughter, using hand tracking to pick up objects, write letters and handle word cards in speech-therapy scenes, some of which are designed to fail at first. It is based on the story of co-director Marion Burger's father.

title: Endangered Gestures
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Text / print
summary: A short film (4K single-channel video, 6'10'') and artist book (Small Book of Endangered Gestures) showing hand gestures generated with AI imaging for words and phrases that began disappearing from U.S. government websites, documents and archives in March 2025. Each censored word is paired with a proposed gesture made by hands that are almost but not quite human. It received a Prix Ars Electronica Honorary Mention (New Animation Art) and was shortlisted for the LUMA Rencontres Dummy Book Award in 2026.

title: Energy Field
summary: A studio album (CD and digital, Touch TO:73, released April 2010) of three tracks, about 50 minutes, composed from hydrophone and microphone recordings Winderen made in the Barents Sea, Greenland and Norway, including inside glacier crevasses, in fjords and in the open ocean. Listeners hear layered underwater and shoreline sound, among it crustaceans and fish such as cod, haddock, herring and pollock, as well as wind, ravens and dogs. It won the Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2011.

title: Epiphyte Chamber
media: Material / sculpture | Robotics / kinetics | Sensor / interaction
summary: Epiphyte Chamber is an installation of linked masses, described as 'floating islands', hung from above. Each is built from thousands of lightweight, digitally fabricated components that move together in subtle, coordinated, nearly synchronised 'breathing and whispers'. Visitors walk into enclosed sculptural spaces among them, which connect to larger gathering areas. Philip Beesley Architect Inc. (PBAI) made it for the inaugural Aleph Exhibition at the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul (12 November 2013 - 16 March 2014). It received an Honorary Mention for Interactive Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

title: Estate (July 10, 2022)
media: AI / generative | Camera / computer vision | Material / sculpture
summary: Estate (July 10, 2022) is a sculpture in the form of a door intercom mounted on a folding screen, shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026. A camera in the work monitors its surroundings, and an AI model trained on the social media posts of a deceased person from a creative field speaks in a cloned voice when visitors come near, responding with fragments of recollection (for example a recipe when someone passes holding a drink). An LED screen counts the years, days, hours and minutes since that person's death.

title: Eunoia
summary: Eunoia is a performance in which Lisa Park wears a commercial NeuroSky EEG headset while meditating; custom software turns her 'Attention' and 'Meditation' values and brainwave data into sound, adjusting volume, pitch and panning. The sound plays through five speakers under five water-filled metal dishes arranged in a circle around her, so that her mental states appear as vibrations on the water. Her stated aim was to reach a stillness in which no sound is heard and the water does not move.

title: Evaporating Symphony
summary: An installation of 3D-printed metal stones on elevated stainless steel panels at varying heights, heated through heat conductors, thermal sensors, relays and a thermal controller, with roller pumps and water pipes delivering droplets of water. Each droplet that touches a stone evaporates in under a second with a soft percussive sound, which is amplified in the space. It was shown at the 13th Seoul Mediacity Biennale, Séance: Technology of the Spirit, Seoul Museum of Art (2025).

title: Everything
summary: Everything is a video game and nature simulation for PC, Mac, Linux, PlayStation 4 and later Nintendo Switch in which every thing the player sees, from animals and plants to planets and galaxies, can be played as a character; the player moves between scales from the microscopic to the cosmic, and can read the thoughts of other things. It has no tasks, objectives or scores, plays itself if left unattended, and includes recorded talks by the philosopher Alan Watts as narration. Its gameplay film received the 2017 Golden Nica in Prix Ars Electronica's Computer Animation/Film/VFX category and was shown in the CyberArts exhibition at OK Center in Linz.

title: Eyes of Shame (Gėdos akys)
summary: Eyes of Shame is a 40-minute animated virtual reality film (Lithuania, France, Croatia). It follows 14-year-old Eyeless in a hospital for troubled teenagers: when a nurse forces her to eat, unfinished memories begin to interrupt the present, and the viewer is placed in her point of view. It premiered in the Venice Immersive competition in 2026 and draws on the director's volunteering at a hospital for teenagers in Vilnius, where he has run animation workshops since 2014.

title: F*ckai? (Famous)
summary: F*ckai? (Famous) is a five-minute 3D-animated short film by Toronto director and animator Jordan Clarke. Its story, about an AI that wanted to be famous, was generated by OpenAI in response to his prompt and voiced by an AI, then paraphrased and edited by Clarke, who animated, composited, sound-designed and edited the film himself. It closes his 'f*ckai?' series of short films and received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at the 2024 Prix Ars Electronica.

title: Facial Weaponization Suite
media: Material / sculpture | Camera / computer vision | Performance / body
summary: A series of community workshops in which participants' faces are scanned and the aggregated facial data is modelled into amorphous "collective masks" that biometric facial recognition does not detect as human faces. The masks are used in public interventions and performances and shown with videos and prints; individual masks address queer men's faces (Fag Face Mask), blackness, feminism and veil legislation, and biometrics at the Mexico-US border.

title: fake synthetic music
summary: Fake Synthetic Music is a live performance for voice, echo, lights and spatial distribution, and a double LP released on PAN in 2018. Janvin sings sustained and sequenced tones through an amplified microphone and a digital echo, imitating synthetic sounds, while programmed lights accompany the performance. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: Fashion Show for Elders
summary: Fashion Show for Elders is a series of AI-generated images by Nigerian filmmaker Malik Afegbua showing elderly African models on a runway in outfits mixing traditional Nigerian dress with futuristic designs. The show never took place: the models and clothes were produced with several AI image generators, and the images were shared online, where many viewers took them for a real event.

title: FEARDEATHLOVEDEATH
summary: A 17-minute film shot on Super 16mm and transferred to Full HD, commissioned by Röda Sten Konsthall, Gothenburg. It is divided into chapters: the contents of a recently deceased man's bedroom described in an invented one-word language, an abstract time-based painting sequence, a love poem, and an alligator appearing in the clouds. Viewers watch it as a single-channel film in screenings and exhibitions.

title: Foragers
summary: A film of about an hour combining documentary, scripted fiction and archival footage, shot mainly in the Galilee, the Golan Heights and around Jerusalem. It follows Palestinian foragers gathering za'atar and 'akkoub, plants whose wild harvesting is restricted under Israeli nature-protection law, and stages court hearings co-scripted with lawyer Rabea Eghbariah. Viewers watch it as a film in cinemas, festivals and exhibitions.

title: Forms
media: Projection | Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision
summary: A video work and installation by Quayola and Memo Akten made from archive footage of athletes (swimmers, divers, pole vaulters, gymnasts), whose movements are tracked and used to drive physics-based simulations that become abstract moving sculptures. In the National Media Museum installation (Bradford, 2012) the animation was projected on a large screen, with a smaller screen showing the source footage and the individual layers. It received the Golden Nica for Computer Animation / Film / VFX at Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: frequencies (a)
summary: frequencies (a) is a sound and light performance in which tuning forks mounted in small acrylic structures on a lighting table are struck by computer-controlled solenoids, each fork linked to a contact microphone and a light. Bernier sequences the strikes, digital sounds and light pulses with Ableton Live and Max for Live, and the audience sits close to the table as the setup alternates between darkness and white light. It is the first part of Bernier's frequencies series and received the 2013 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: From Hand to Mouth
summary: An installation of steel, glass, a workshop crane, tubes and a pump in which a glass fermenter holds a replica of the right hand of Michelangelo's David, 3D-printed in the bioplastic PHB. PHB-producing bacteria (including Cupriavidus necator) in the fermenter gradually metabolise the hand and alter its form. It belongs to chapter 5 of Feuerstein's METABOLICA project and was shown in Renaissance 3.0 at ZKM Karlsruhe (2023), whose collection holds it.

title: From Noise
media: AI / generative | Network / data | Text / print
summary: From Noise is a series of 12 NFTs from one algorithm by Tyler Hobbs that translates the spontaneous gestural marks of painters such as Cy Twombly and Joan Mitchell into code; each work contains more than 4,000 marks. At Zero 10, Art Basel Miami Beach 2025 (SOLOS stand), it was shown as four large-format prints on wood varnished by the artist, with boxed sets of screen prints, Translated Gestures, taken from details of the outputs.

title: fugue notes
summary: fugue notes is a film (HD digital video and 16mm, with sound) in which the artist's original plan for a film is replaced by its notes: in deep shadow and darkness, a voiceover links eroding autobiographical memory with the failed image. It was commissioned by CIRCUIT for Leap to the Place of Two Pools at Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery, Wellington (2025), and was later screened at Artspace Aotearoa in 2026 with the artist reading the script live.

title: FuneralPlay
summary: A website presented as a fictitious online funeral platform where mourners attend simulated funerals for lost loved ones in themed virtual mausoleums, such as a mahjong room, a gallery of cat memes or a feng shui master's orchard. Users can choose to delete a deceased person's digital footprint, keep it as an inheritance, or donate it to a collective Memorial Hall, and can give NFTs as memorial gifts; exploring a scene reveals hidden clues and rewards. The platform states it has no actual financial function and does not share data with other platforms.

title: Garden of the Broken Hearted
summary: An installation in the Arsenale at the 61st Venice Biennale (In Minor Keys): a large olive tree placed on a rotating stage, onto which a video is projected. The projected footage shows the same tree, filmed before its transport to Venice.

title: GR-AI-N
media: Robotics / kinetics | Camera / computer vision | Material / sculpture
summary: GR-AI-N is a digital-craft workflow that uses discarded offcuts from the wood industry: pieces are scanned, AI-powered tools extract their grain patterns, texture and imperfections, and robotic assembly and milling build objects (mirrors, a headboard) as 3D mosaics of irregular pieces that keep the grain continuous. It was developed in the VOJEXT S+T+ARTS residency 'Robotics in Arts and Crafts' in Barcelona and was nominated for the 2024 S+T+ARTS Prize.

title: Grisaille
media: VR / AR / XR | Projection | Performance / body
summary: Grisaille is a two-part mixed-reality painting experience by Teek Mach, with composer Joel Douek, performed in the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier section from 25 January to 2 February 2019. In part one a visitor puts on an Oculus Go headset in a dark hallway and moves through a virtual copy of it, past a hologram of the artist and a series of her hand-painted VR portraits; in part two the artist, present in the room, draws the visitor's silhouette with Tilt Brush on an HTC Vive Pro, projected live onto the wall and joined to the silhouettes of earlier visitors, while Douek layers festival sounds with original music. Mach performed it eleven hours a day for the nine days of the festival.

title: Grosse Fatigue
summary: Grosse Fatigue is a 13-minute colour video with sound in which overlapping computer windows show footage filmed in the collections of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., mixed with images found on the internet and scenes filmed in places such as a pet store and a domestic interior. Over the images a spoken-word poem, written with Jacob Bromberg and voiced by Akwetey Orraca-Tetteh, combines scientific history with creation stories from religious, hermetic and oral traditions. It was made during a Smithsonian Artist Research Fellowship and presented at the 55th Venice Biennale, Il Palazzo Enciclopedico, in 2013.

title: Guanaquerx
summary: Guanaquerx is a four-legged robot modelled on the guanaco, partly made from caña colihue bamboo and dressed in Andean textiles. In January 2024, about 30 people with 58 mules and horses took it across the Andes from Argentina to the Chilean border over seven days, re-enacting the 1817 crossing by San Martín's army; mules carried the robot where the ground was too rough for it. The robot records sound and images, emits a synthetic whinny, beats a drum, waves a flag and carries a plaque with 'Pluriversal Laws of Robotics'. The work won the 2025 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2025.

title: Hand-Me-Downs
summary: Hand-Me-Downs is a film in which Yto Barrada narrates sixteen family 'myths' over strangers' home movies and archival films from the last half-century in Morocco. According to the Walker Art Center, the footage is Super 8 home movies found at Moroccan flea markets; Barrada says the material came to her through a French archive of amateur and propaganda films. It was made for RIFFS, her Deutsche Bank Artist of the Year 2011 exhibition, which travelled to Ikon Gallery, Birmingham, in 2012.

title: HANDMADE
summary: HANDMADE is a video diptych of about 11 minutes, originally conceived for two 4K monitors and presented at MoMA from November 2023 in the ground-floor Gund Lobby on a large media wall. One part shows digitally manipulated footage of a gale-force storm on Lake Huron, filmed by Thornton with a handheld camera while lying down; the other shows a physicist at Caltech making a handwoven sensing device for a research project on antimatter. These are interspersed with film recordings of fluid-dynamics studies that Thornton found during her 2019 residency in the Caltech-Huntington Program in Visual Culture.

title: Harvesting Climate Action
media: Material / sculpture | Network / data | Online / net art
summary: Harvesting Climate Action was a six-week installation in Hackney Service Centre, London (autumn 2025), part of Ling Tan's Low Carbon Chinatown project, made with Hackney Council's Climate Team. Its centre was 100 recyclable cardboard stools, each printed on one side with a 'Climate Action' (from individual to borough-wide) and on the other with the carbon footprint of a meal ingredient, alongside data maps, food-making videos, audio stories and living produce. The installation then became a 'Low Carbon Banquet for a Hundred', where 100 members of the public each took a stool, sat with strangers over low carbon East and Southeast Asian dishes, debated and voted on the actions, and took their stool home; the 100 Climate Actions also exist as an online toolkit. It received an Honorary Mention (Digital Humanity) at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Hero
media: VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture | Sound
summary: Hero is a large-scale, multi-sensory 'vérité' virtual-reality installation by iNK Stories (Navid and Vassiliki Khonsari), produced with Starbreeze, set in a Syrian town during and after a barrel-bomb air raid. Participants wear a VR headset and haptic backpack and walk through a built set whose props (a tire, crates, bricks) mirror the virtual space, with smell, heat, vibration and surround sound; the session lasts about seven minutes and is followed by a recovery room. Syrian refugees placed in the U.S. by ICNA Relief were interviewed and photographed for the piece; it premiered in Sundance New Frontier in January 2018 and was shown at Tribeca Immersive in April 2018.

title: Hidirtina / Sisters
summary: Hidirtina / Sisters is a 9'14" animated video based on a myth from Eritrea and northern Ethiopia about seven immortal sisters living in nature and a hunter who kills a deer, is cursed, and is protected by a piece of a tree until he loses it in a river. The story was told to the artist by a volunteer who answered his open call for folklore to a Habesha diaspora community in New York, and the animation also includes the process of its making, such as email exchanges, café meetings and a brief portrait of the storyteller. It was shown in the 21st Contemporary Art Biennial Sesc_Videobrasil, 'Imagined Communities' (São Paulo, 2019–20).

title: Hinat
summary: A multi-panel installation made during an AlUla residency in 2022, named after Hinat, a Nabataean woman whose tomb (Tomb 117) is at Hegra. Painted and photo-transferred collages of AlUla landscapes have rectangles cut out, into which videos are projected; the videos, generated with machine learning from footage of three women from AlUla wearing coloured fabrics, show ghostly figures moving across the landscapes. It was shown in 'Art of the Kingdom' at the Saudi Arabian Museum of Contemporary Art.

title: Holly+
media: Sound | AI / machine learning | Network / data
summary: A public website where anyone can upload audio and get it back 'sung' in a machine-learning model of Holly Herndon's voice, built with Never Before Heard Sounds. What people make is theirs to use; 'official' Holly+ works are voted on by a DAO of stewards, sold as NFTs, with profits split between the maker, the DAO treasury and Herndon.

title: Home
summary: Home is a two-channel (diptych) video installation drawn from the artist's extended conversations with Anonya (also spelled Anonnya), a transgender woman from Dhaka. It was made in Dhaka in 2014 for the group exhibition Cross Casting, curated by Mahbubur Rahman at Britto Arts Trust, an artist-run space Lipi co-founded. Her meeting with Anonya while making the video led to the 2015 exhibition Reversal Reality (Shrine Empire, New Delhi), which compared the two women's childhoods through video, photographs and objects.

title: Homeland
summary: Homeland is a 10-minute HD video by Halil Altındere, commissioned and co-produced by the 9th Berlin Biennale (2016), with voice and lyrics by the Syrian rapper and activist Mohammad Abu Hajar and music by Nguzunguzu. Abu Hajar's song accompanies scenes of refugees' journeys, partly based on real-life footage and partly staged, from a border crossing to the waterways of Istanbul and ending at the former Tempelhof airport in Berlin, then used as a refugee camp. It was later shown at the 13th Bienal de Artes Mediales in Santiago.

title: Homo Machina (Human Machine, a.k.a. Gay Machine)
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision
summary: A life-size sculptural digital console shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026. It combines sculpture with video and surveillance footage and functions as a self-portrait. The neon-green surface carries a cast face and 3D-printed parts, and at its centre a clear womb holds a motor-driven ouroboros.

title: Honorata
summary: Honorata is a 15-minute multichannel song conceived as a lullaby, commissioned by MUAC for its Espacio de Experimentación Sonora in Mexico City, where it was shown from 11 October 2025 to April 2026. Visitors listen to Nasta's voice with bass, viola, guitar, Rhodes piano, Hammond organ and synthesisers, spatialised across the room's 22 channels by Tobías Álvarez. The piece was composed during Nasta's pregnancy and finished a few months after the birth.

title: Horn Orchestra
summary: Horn Orchestra is a sound installation of ten car horns suspended in an enclosed space. Silent when no one is there, it is triggered by the presence of visitors who walk into the space and then sounds at random. It won the Léopold Sédar Senghor Grand Prize at the Dak'Art Biennale in Dakar in May 2012.

title: Hotel Infinity
summary: Hotel Infinity is a room-scale VR puzzle game by Studio Chyr, set in a hotel built from non-Euclidean, looping architecture. Players move through hallways and ballrooms by physically walking inside a play area of about 2 x 2 metres, with portals folding the space, and solve puzzles to uncover the hotel's secrets. It was released for Meta Quest and PS VR2 on 13 November 2025 and selected for Venice Immersive 2026.

title: huě iànn
artist: Yu-Han Chen, Ching-Wen Hsu, Ruei-Sin Jhang, Li-Hua Zhan, Tung-En Chien, Pei-Chi Wu
summary: huě iànn is a VR animated video made by a six-person team from the Department of Visual Communication Design at Jinwen University of Science and Technology, Taiwan. It addresses events in Taiwan's history connected to freedom of speech, starting from the Taiyuan incident. It received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: I Am Your Grandma
media: Online / net art | Screen / monitor | Performance / body
summary: I Am Your Grandma is a short music video in which Jillian Mayer addresses her unborn grandchildren, appearing in a series of costumes, masks and make-up while she mouths a song repeating 'I am your grandma' (music by Michael John Hancock). It was first shown in her solo exhibition Family Matters at David Castillo Gallery, Miami, in April 2011, and then posted on YouTube, where it was watched millions of times. Wikipedia lists it as a short film made with Lucas Leyva.

title: I DIDNT REALISE YOU THOUGHT LIKE THAT
summary: An online game for web and mobile, released by Serpentine on 21 May 2026, in which players decide whether to open a door to fictional characters, conspiracy agents or 'Influencers' who ask to enter on the basis of their stated beliefs. The game simulates a real-time feed, and players meet a cast of characters and reach different endings depending on their choices. It is described as the next chapter of THE DELUSION, the multiplayer game exhibition at Serpentine North (September 2025 to January 2026), where a gallery version with a transparent door and a screen was the first work visitors encountered.

title: I Saw Square Triangle Sine
summary: An installation made for Camden Arts Centre (7 October 2011 – 8 January 2012) that brings together band instruments – a keyboard, drum kit and synthesisers – with turntables, LED lighting, lamps and radios to produce a minimal audio composition. It includes paintings from Angus Fairhurst's Underdone / Overdone Paintings (1998) with a drum kit, and visitors can play the drums, adding their own noise or rhythm to the installation. The work toured to Spike Island, Bristol, in 2012.

title: I'm Feeling Lucky
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: A real-time generative installation of infinite runtime in which a historically and geographically ambiguous 3D landscape, generated with game engine technology, is populated with thousands of figures taken from Google Street View and turned into 3D models by a deep neural network. A virtual camera pans endlessly across the landscape, a format the artist relates to 19th-century panorama paintings; a 360° fulldome version (Panorama: I'm Feeling Lucky) was shown at the SAT in Montréal. Sound design and composition by Tatum Wilson.

title: I'm Humanity
summary: I'm Humanity is a pop song by Etsuko Yakushimaru released in 2016 as a digital download, on CD and as a genetically modified microorganism: the song's main chord progression was converted through a codon-based cipher into a 276-nucleotide DNA sequence and inserted into the genome of the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, which copies it with each cell division.
