The microorganism was exhibited at KENPOKU ART 2016 in Ibaraki and at YCAM in Yamaguchi, where the song was also performed live by her band Soutaiseiriron with a section arranged to resemble mutation. It received the STARTS Prize 2017 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration.

title: I.AM.ISIGO Digital Mystery System
media: Online / net art | Network / data | Material / sculpture
summary: A digital tool by Bubu Ogisi's label I.AM.ISIGO that archives knowledge of African weaving techniques gathered through research with artisan communities, and lets users create new weaving patterns. It was shown in the S+T+ARTS exhibition at Ars Electronica Festival 2024 in the context of the STARTS4Africa project.

title: If You Have Starry Skies in Your Eyes
summary: A prosthetic eye designed, made and worn by the artist, who lost the sight of her right eye as a child; it contains a magnetic sensor, an LED and a battery encapsulated in medical-grade acrylic resin, and lights up when a magnet is brought near. The project, presented with a video, follows an earlier starry-sky-patterned prosthetic eye she wears daily, and received an Award of Distinction in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: IGÚN
summary: An ongoing series of StyleGAN models trained on images of Benin Bronzes looted from the Benin Kingdom during the 1897 British invasion, now held in museum collections. It generates synthetic prototypes of objects that might have been cast during the 17-year interregnum (1897–1914), when no Oba commissioned work; datasets were extended with ceremonial heads in wood and pottery because there were too few bronze images to train the model. The Lumen Prize presentation shows video of latent-space interpolations; the work won the Lumen Prize Global South Award in 2021.

title: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation)
summary: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation) is a single-visitor booth in which the visitor is shown a piece of missile shrapnel the artist collected on front lines in Ukraine. The visitor's presence and physiological signals, including heartbeat, are picked up without contact and shape a low-frequency soundscape. The title refers to the roughly 36,000 fragments a fragmentation weapon breaks into; the booth is a variation of an ongoing project, shown in the IDFA DocLab Competition 2025, with a larger walk-through version in development.

title: In a Small Room
media: AI / generative | VR / AR / XR | Screen / monitor
summary: A project titled in full 'In a Small Room: The Gap between Advertising and Reality', made as a Royal College of Art (Information Experience Design) degree project, about cramped housing in London and Seoul and the advertising images used to rent it. It has four parts: an interactive web application (CycleGAN) into which visitors put a photo of a real room and receive an advertising-style image, a VR installation of an 'advertising' room entered from a bed in a built room, two films shot in the same Seoul goshiwon room (a documentary and an advertisement), and a research dissertation. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Humanity at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: In Cameras Res
media: Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision | Network / data
summary: In Cameras Res is a three-channel moving-image installation by CAMP, commissioned by De Appel, Amsterdam, for which automated CCTV (pan-tilt-zoom) cameras were programmed to film landscape sequences of the city. Each film was shot from a single camera position on a historical building (the former Royal Dutch Shell headquarters, now A'DAM Tower; the former NHM building, now Stadsarchief Amsterdam; the former Tetterode printing foundry), each with a distinct editing technique, and certain people recur in the frame. It was shown at De Appel from 16 March to 20 April 2019.

title: In Potentia
summary: In Potentia is an installation in which human foreskin cells are reprogrammed with the induced pluripotent stem cell (iPS) technique into stem cells and then into neurons, forming a living neural network kept in a purpose-built sculptural incubator with an automated feeding and waste system. A multi-electrode array records the network's electrical activity and converts it into sound, so visitors listen to the neural culture rather than see it, as the cells are not visible to the naked eye. It was made with Stuart Hodgetts and Mark Lawson and shown at Kibla, Maribor (2012) and at ISEA2013, Powerhouse Museum, Sydney, among other venues.

title: In Search of Vanished Blood
summary: In Search of Vanished Blood is a room-filling video/shadow play commissioned by dOCUMENTA (13) in 2012: six synchronised films are projected through five rotating Mylar cylinders reverse-painted with figures of soldiers, animals, gods and guns, so that moving images and shadows pass over the walls, floor and visitors. A soundscape, voiced and designed by the artist, speaks from the perspective of Cassandra and draws on texts by Faiz Ahmed Faiz, Christa Wolf, Mahasweta Devi, Samuel Beckett and Heiner Müller. The title comes from a 1965 Urdu poem by Faiz; a single-channel video version is in the M+ collection, Hong Kong.

title: In Vitro
summary: In Vitro is a two-channel, Arabic-language, black-and-white science-fiction film (about 28 minutes) by Larissa Sansour, co-directed with Søren Lind, commissioned by the Danish Arts Foundation for the Danish Pavilion at the 58th Venice Biennale (2019), where it was shown with the sculpture Monument for Lost Time under the title Heirloom. Set after an eco-disaster, it takes place in an abandoned nuclear reactor under Bethlehem converted into an orchard, where scientists prepare to replant the soil with heirloom seeds. The film is a dialogue between the dying founder of the bunker, Dunia, and her successor Alia, who was born underground and carries memories implanted in her.

title: Intercourses
summary: Intercourses is a five-channel film installation made for the Danish Pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale (1 June - 24 November 2013). The film was shot in Tianducheng, a replica of Paris in a suburb of Hangzhou, China, and follows three men moving through the city, with the city itself treated as the main character. Projections of different sizes were placed through the pavilion, and architectural interventions began outside the building before visitors entered.

title: Interface I
summary: A kinetic installation in which 192 DC motors in two facing rows pull vertical strings against each other like a tug of war, while a mesh of red elastic bands couples each string to its neighbours. The motors are driven by random impulses from Geiger-Müller tubes that register natural background radiation, so the shape of the mesh keeps shifting without a programmed choreography. Visitors watch the band network move as the opposing forces push it up or down. The work was first shown as Order+Noise (Interface I) at NOME Gallery, Berlin, in 2016.

title: Interlooped
artist: Maria Guta, Robin Mange, Javier Bello Ruiz, FlexFab
media: VR / AR / XR | Camera / computer vision | Performance / body
summary: Interlooped is a multi-user mixed-reality installation and live performance in which the visitor, wearing a VR headset, is captured in real time as a low-resolution volumetric (voxel) hologram by depth-sensor cameras, using technology by the Geneva company Imverse. The visitor's movements and those of performer Maria Guta are recorded and replayed as time loops, so the virtual room fills with multiple versions of both; in a second part Guta joins live, dressed as in the recordings. It premiered in New Frontier at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2019.

title: Island Waters
summary: A 60-second animated video projection-mapped onto the facade of CHIJMES at the Singapore Night Festival 2025 (22 Aug-6 Sep), commissioned by the National Heritage Board and made by illustrator and motion designer Lim KangLi in the festival's Projection Mapping Masterclass. The animation moves from a ripple down to the seabed, up through maritime routes and back to the surface, with colours drawn from Peranakan porcelain.

title: Iyeza
summary: Iyeza is an 11-minute film, written and directed by Kudzanai Chiurai, described in the Sundance programme as an allegory of the Last Supper depicting the establishment of a new nation-state, setting the past and the present of a continent in civil wars side by side. It is in Xhosa with English subtitles, with music by Thandiswa Mazwai. Chiurai says it is one of three films (Iyeza, Creation and Moyo) about birth, sacrifice and death. It screened at the 2013 Sundance Film Festival and at MIFF 2013 in Melbourne.

title: Justin
summary: Over three months Ang Song Ming practised copying the signature of pop musician Justin Bieber, then signed Bieber's autograph on a poster of the musician. The installation consists of 34 practice sheets, a slide projector showing 80 35mm slides, and the signed, framed poster, documenting the change from the artist's own handwriting to Bieber's. The work is in the Singapore Art Museum collection.

title: K-9_topology
summary: K-9_topology is a series of four projects (2014–2017) about the relationship between humans, dogs and wolves: Ecce Canis (a fragrance made from serotonin of the artist and her dog), I Hunt Nature and Culture Hunts Me (a performance made during a residency at JACANA Wildlife Studios in France, on the relationship between wolf, dog and human), Hybrid Family (a three-month seclusion in which the artist induced lactation and lived with her dogs, ending in a public performance with a puppy) and ARTE_mis (a hybrid cell made by fusing the artist's enucleated egg cell with a somatic cell of her dog, shown frozen under a microscope). For the 2017 CyberArts exhibition in Linz the series was shown together as an installation in the form of a dog stacker, a training tool for show dogs.

title: khalil
summary: khalil is a site-specific multimedia installation by Khaled Sabsabi in In Minor Keys, the main exhibition of the 61st Venice Biennale (2026), made of object, video, scent and sound. Its title is the Arabic word for close friend or companion. Sabsabi showed it at the same time as conference of one's self in the Australia Pavilion, and he describes the two as complementary works.

title: Kissing of the Threshold
summary: Kissing of the Threshold (Urdu: آستان بوس) is a project by Fazal Rizvi centred on Shia traditions of mourning and remembrance, shown as a new commission at Sharjah Biennial 16 (2025). Dawn's review describes a large-scale installation with buckets of water, a mound representing a grave, and an eight-channel audio work in which the artist's voice recites soz; the Sharjah Art Foundation also published it as a two-part artist book of calligraphy and performative photographs referring to the Ghusaals in Pakistan, who wash and prepare the bodies of the dead.

title: Knit II
summary: Knit II (2021) is a 4K video by Kawita Vatanajyankur, listed on the Simon Lee Foundation Institute of Contemporary Asian Art (AGWA) artist page. It belongs to her knitting works within the Performing Textiles series, in which the artist uses her own body as the mechanism of a knitting machine, weaving red yarn into a web-like fabric on camera. Viewers watch the recorded performance as a video.

title: Korean Internet Tour Guide
artist: E Roon Kang, Achim Koh and Wonyoung So
media: Online / net art | Text / print | Network / data
summary: A research project commissioned by SeMA Biennale Mediacity Seoul 2016, consisting of a website (k-www.kr), a booklet and two related programs. The website lists "tourist attractions" collected from the Korean internet with related essays, starting from two interface software particular to Korea, ActiveX and Zeroboard; selected content was published as a book and displayed at the Biennale.

title: kus
summary: kus (2025) is an installation with audio shown at the Aichi Arts Center (8F) in Aichi Triennale 2025, made by travelling between Mayunkiki's hometown of Asahikawa, Hokkaido, and the Tenryu River basin. Her team recorded sounds of present-day railways and the natural environment and overlapped them with recordings of traditional Ainu song. The work draws on the history of her grandfather Kawamura Kaneto, an Ainu leader and surveying engineer who supervised railway construction between Tenryukyo and Mikawa-Kawai, and was presented together with her performance work kuste.

title: Kwaku Ananse
summary: Kwaku Ananse is a short film (about 25 minutes; Ghana, Mexico, USA) that combines semi-autobiographical elements with the West African tale of Kwaku Ananse, a trickster who appears as both spider and man. Nyan, a young Ghanaian-American woman, travels to Ghana for the funeral of her estranged father, who had a second family there, and after the funeral goes into the forest in search of his spirit. It premiered in Berlinale Shorts at the 2013 Berlin International Film Festival.

title: L'Onde du Midi
summary: L'Onde du Midi is a permanent kinetic sculpture commissioned by the Musée du Louvre and inaugurated in January 2020 above the Escalier du Midi (Sully wing). It consists of 128 aluminium tubes suspended from nearly invisible cables driven by motors; computer-programmed sequences move the roughly 10-metre horizontal plane in slow undulations between 3 and 4.5 metres high. Visitors on the staircase watch the shifting configurations.

title: La laguna parla
summary: La laguna parla is a 35-minute collective, smartphone-guided ritual about the Venice lagoon, water and collective power, made for the tenth anniversary of Venice Immersive (2026), in which hundreds of participants take part with their own phones. It is an adaptation of The Waterbodies Orchestra, an earlier work by The Confluence of European Water Bodies and The Smartphone Orchestra made to give a voice to European water bodies. In Smartphone Orchestra experiences, participants receive instructions, prompts, questions and games on their phones that lead them to interact with the other people in the room.

title: La vida en rojo
summary: La vida en rojo is a 21'50" video essay (2016-2018) by Julia Mensch, part of a long-term project begun in 2008 about the private and political life of her grandparents, both members of the Argentinian Communist Party. A narrating voice contextualises and questions images of the grandparents' house, slides from her grandfather's 1970s trip through the Soviet bloc, letters, postcards and photographs from the family archive. It was shown at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil, Imagined Communities (São Paulo, 2019-2020).

title: Labor
summary: Labor is a self-regulating installation in which three glass bioreactors, each incubating one species of human skin bacteria (Staphylococcus epidermidis, Corynebacterium xerosis, Propionibacterium avidum), produce the smell of sweating, stressed bodies without any people involved. The scents combine in a central chamber holding a white T-shirt, and a Raspberry Pi-based system of stirrers, sensors, pumps, heaters and valves runs the process; the installation also includes sweat-stain-transfer prints.

title: Laboratorio de invención social (o posibles formas de construcción colectiva)
summary: A four-channel video installation from Gabriela Golder's series Reoccupation, made with workers of three Argentine cooperatives in recovered factories (Cintoplom, Cadenas Ancla and Cristales San Justo): two channels show the factory (42'20" each) and two show the workers (31'02" each), and the original installation also included printed newspapers. Visitors see and hear images and audio recordings of workers involved in the factory occupations and cooperatives. It received the main award (Estado da Arte – Eletrica Cinema e Vídeo) at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil in 2019.

title: Language Producing Factory
summary: A video installation about NüShu, a script used only by women in villages of Jiangyong County, Hunan, made after the artist's research visits there in 2015–16. In a dungeon-like room three women, their plaited hair pulled by strings held by a female boss, embroider ordered letters onto cloth until they are trapped inside it and sold with the embroidery as a product; the video ends with a glimpse of the real landscape and women of Jiangyong County. It received an Excellence Award in the Art Division of the 21st Japan Media Arts Festival.

title: Laundry Nocturne
summary: Laundry Nocturne (2026) is a multi-channel video projection with field recordings, shown in Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice, the Hong Kong collateral exhibition of the 61st Venice Biennale curated by the Hong Kong Museum of Art. Silhouettes of laundry hung between buildings are projected in the room in a way that simulates moonlight entering through the space's windows. A soundtrack of night-time recordings from Hong Kong, including a wastewater treatment plant, a newspaper-printing facility and a postal sorting centre, plays from a radio in the room.

title: Le Miroir
summary: Le Miroir is an experimental film produced at Le Fresnoy – Studio national des arts contemporains, in which the artist interacts with her own virtual double, a MetaHuman generated from her appearance, in mental landscapes structured around figures inspired by psychoanalytic archetypes (Ego, Superego, Id, Self). It combines real-time 3D animation, motion capture, photogrammetry, miniature sets and filmed sequences, with a soundtrack of synthesizers and electroacoustic composition. It was shown in Le Fresnoy's Panorama 27 and received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Lead the Way
summary: Lead the Way is a triptych made from the physical and audiovisual remains of collaborative performances in Dakar, Johannesburg and Karlsruhe within the project Digital Imaginaries (2018), dedicated to the damaged South African satellite SumbandilaSat, whose Venda name means 'lead the way'. At ZKM Karlsruhe the installation is a shadowscape of ritual objects, Chinese consumer-electronics junk and the shadows of visitors and performers, with robotic lights that pan the space and at times follow the satellite's path. Earlier iterations were a five-hour shadow performance with musician Lamine Kora Kouyaté and dancer Fatou Cissé in Dakar and a video and shadow installation with poets in Johannesburg.

title: lifepatch - citizen initiative in art, science and technology
summary: A community-based, cross-disciplinary organisation in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, formed on 26 March 2012, that runs workshops, research projects and a citizen lab in art, science and technology (e.g. fermentation, DIY electronics, webcam microscopes, Jogja River Project water sampling) and documents its activities on an open wiki. It received an Honorary Mention in the Digital Communities category of Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

title: Light and Belief
summary: Light and Belief: Sketches of Life from the Vietnam War is an installation commissioned by dOCUMENTA (13), Kassel, 2012, that pairs about 100 drawings and watercolours made by artists who served as military painters in the North Vietnamese Army with a 35-minute video of interviews Lê conducted with them. The video, punctuated by animated sequences, records the artists' recollections in relation to their drawings, which depict soldiers' portraits and everyday moments between battles. Sets of the work were later shown at the Carnegie International (2013), the Mori Art Museum (2015) and Asia Society, New York (2017).

title: Light Keeper
summary: A GPS-enabled sound walk and light installation commissioned for Singapore Biennale 2025 at Fort Canning Park. Visitors use a GPS-enabled app that guides them to five sites in the park, where audio vignettes based on the artists' encounters with lighthouses, lighthouse keepers and crypto-linguists play; at the Fort Canning Lighthouse, a programmed, looped light cycle runs after dusk. A companion three-channel video, Light Keeper: Signal (2025, 7 min 58 sec), is shown at Fort Canning Centre.

title: Lines of Divergence
summary: Lines of Divergence is a 7'35" video documenting a current land occupation near Pucusana, a fishing village on the outskirts of Lima, where chalk lines drawn in the desert divide newly registered land into plots. It is the last chapter of the artist's documentation, begun in 2010, of the bamboo-and-wood structures built in the desert to claim land, a process often called 'invasions' that has shaped Peru's coast since the 1950s. Her 2018 solo exhibition at Galerie Gisela Capitain, Cologne, was titled Lines of Divergence, and the video was shown at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019).

title: Liquid Crystal
summary: A Whitney artport commission of seven short videos, one for each day of the week, shown on whitney.org at sunrise and sunset in New York (Apr–Jul 2023). Each video opens on a natural surface (leaves and moss, sand, gravel, snow, broken ice) that the artist's hands push aside to reveal a screen of synthesized video patterns.

title: Live Study
media: Online / net art | Performance / body | Screen / monitor
summary: Live Study is an online durational performance commissioned by the Whitney Museum for its artport platform, in which a live video stream (2019–2024, now an archive) showed Michael Mandiberg painting portraits of the people who had worked for the artist over the years. Each canvas is sized at one square inch per hour the person worked; many portraits were painted twice, one priced at the total wages Mandiberg paid the subject and the other given to the subject. Visitors to the artport site browse the archived livestream videos of the painting sessions alongside the 100 resulting paintings and studies.

title: Loophole for All
media: Online / net art | Network / data | Text / print
summary: Loophole for All is an online intervention in which the artist exposed over 200,000 companies registered in the Cayman Islands, leaking their names from the government registry, and offered the identities of these anonymous offshore companies for low-cost sale on the website Loophole4All.com, issuing forged Certificates of Incorporation under his own name and signature. He also set up his own company in the City of London and produced a video documentary of interviews with experts on offshore centres. In exhibitions the work is shown as two video channels and digital prints of the certificates and legal documents, with a flowchart of the operation.

title: Lost in Trans(mission)
summary: Lost in Trans(mission) is a 2015 video by the Nairobi-based artist Jackie Karuti. It was shown in her first solo exhibition, Labyrinth, at Kuona Trust Arts Centre in Nairobi in January 2015, together with the installation Exit (a door that opens onto a blank wall) and mixed-media paintings of figures behind prison bars. The video and the door installation were later included in the group exhibition Entry Prohibited to Foreigners in Sweden.

title: Love Birds, Night Birds, Devil-Birds
artist: Cassie McQuater (original music by Kelly Moran)
summary: Love Birds, Night Birds, Devil-Birds is a nonlinear fairy tale made as an interactive video game installation and as a multi-channel video, with original music by Kelly Moran. It starts from Leonora Carrington's story 'The Debutante', in which a young woman exchanges places with a hyena masked in human skin, and shows dresses made of anatomical parts, glass and pink light moving through landscapes of fluorescent flowers, monsters and deconstructed birds. It debuted as a three-channel video installation in TRANSFER Gallery's series 'The Download', was released as a single-channel video with Warp Records, and won the Lumen Prize Moving Image Award in 2019.

title: Love Story
summary: Love Story is a seven-channel video installation based on day-long interviews with six people who fled their countries and were seeking or had been granted asylum in Berlin, New York or Cape Town. In a first room, actors Alec Baldwin and Julianne Moore re-perform fragments of the interviews on a green-screen set in a fast-cut montage; a second room, reachable only through the first, shows the six original interviews in full.

title: Mad Horse City
media: Screen / monitor | VR / AR / XR | Text / print
summary: Mad Horse City is a collaboration between architect-artist Olalekan Jeyifous and writer Wale Lawal that imagines Lagos in the year 2115 through three fictional 'moments' – Offline, Òmìníra and Dreamscape – presented as experimental animations, a digital slideshow, a 360 VR experience and a graphic novella. In Offline a woman visits an illegal botanical garden where people pay to disconnect; in Òmìníra two scavengers from a fishing community inspired by Makoko test the limits of their society; in Dreamscape a young man illegally downloads the dreams of people in other jurisdictions. It was shown in Africa Is Not a Refugee Camp at the Architekturmuseum der TU München and in Digital Imaginaries at ZKM Karlsruhe (2018–19).

title: Makȟóčhe Kiŋ Oíč'iwa (The Land Paints Itself)
summary: A digital video with sound commissioned by CIRCUIT Artist Moving Image and shown in the group exhibition Leap to the Place of Two Pools at Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery, Wellington (1 February – 6 April 2025). According to the gallery, the work pairs technologies of dreaming and AI to imagine Indigenous futures patterned across unceded land, marked by stones whose own language emerges as a conduit to multivocal storytelling.

title: MANTRAcks and Sonic Fields: A VirtuAural Duology
summary: A long-duration sound piece in two parts made from environmental recordings at two locations. Part 1, untitled #352, uses recordings from an urban boiler plant (RCU) in Fontenay-sous-Bois near Paris and was first developed as the audio-only soundtrack for Anne Collod's choreographic project Exposure, premiered for blindfolded audiences in 2017; part 2, Sonic Fields Vlieland, uses recordings from the North Sea island of Vlieland and was conceived to be listened to at geo-located positions on the island, as a listening walk produced by Soundtrackcity for the Into The Great Wide Open festival. The duology received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: Mapping Uncertain Landscape: The Satellite
media: Robotics / kinetics | Network / data | Text / print
summary: An installation in which a plotter machine built by the artist continuously draws maps of Ukrainian terrain on a large roll of paper, translating vegetation-index data (NDRE/NDVI) from the commercial crop-monitoring satellite EOS SAT into colours. The first version focuses on a road between Ivankiv and the Belarus border; later map series, made with ecologists and earth scientists, follow vegetation changes around the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam (6 June 2023) and the first Russian offensive on Kyiv. It was a diploma project at HEAD Geneva and received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.

title: Maria CHOIR
summary: An interactive installation in which a synthetic reproduction of singer Maria Arnal's voice, produced by models trained on her voice, harmonises in real time with what a visitor sings into a microphone, forming a human-digital choir; an AI-animated avatar responds to the vocal input. Visitors can also record their voice to contribute to a collective synthetic voice model. It was shown in the exhibition AI: Artificial Intelligence at CCCB, Barcelona (18 Oct 2023 – 17 Mar 2024), developed with the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and axolot.cat, and received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.

title: MATER NATVRA (FUTURED PAST series)
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Network / data
summary: A 1/1 edition in digital and physical form, part of the FUTURED PAST series, commissioned for the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach 2025 and shown on the Asprey Studio stand. A digitally sculpted figure of Mother Nature, whose placenta becomes a blind serpent coiled around her leg, was translated into sterling silver by Asprey Studio silversmiths. The digital artwork, issued on a blockchain, is an interactive catalogue in which viewers browse views of the sculpture and a twelve-step creation timeline.

title: Melting Memories
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Melting Memories is a project by Refik Anadol Studio comprising data paintings, augmented data sculptures and light projections made from EEG recordings of participants asked to focus on specific long-term memories, gathered with the Neuroscape Laboratory at the University of California, San Francisco. The data were processed with custom software (VVVV) and recurrent neural nets into moving forms shown on a 5 x 6 metre LED media wall, 65-inch OLED screens and CNC-milled foam pieces. It was exhibited at Pilevneli Gallery, Istanbul, from February to March 2018, and received the Lumen Prize Gold Award in 2019.

title: Memory Melting
summary: Memory Melting is a light installation by Saad Al-Howede shown outside the stc Metro Station at Noor Riyadh 2025. It consists of three large illuminated forms made from discarded plastic toys collected from children around the world and fused together. Some sources describe the forms as spheres and others as oversized emoji shapes.

title: Memory Orbits
summary: A site-specific installation across the five underground rooms of the Barracks at Nasir Bagh, Lahore, commissioned for Lahore Biennale 03 (2024). Visitors descend into the former air-raid bunkers and pass through objects, ceramic sculptures, a mud-dyed suspended cloth, plant material and light and video projections, including a room with forty images of the sun's phases on the curved wall facing a row of forty wax candles. The work is built around the image of an eclipse.

title: MEMORY VAPOR
summary: An installation in which a cloud chamber, combined with a particle accelerator, is illuminated by a scanning white laser sheet. Cosmic-ray particles (ionized nuclei, muons, electrons, positrons) passing through the chamber's supersaturated vapor leave trails of condensation droplets, which the laser turns into points of light that visitors watch.

title: Metachaos
summary: Metachaos is an 8-minute 27-second short film by Alessandro Bavari, made with digitally manipulated photography, animation and a shaky 'camera tremula', in black and white and sepia tones with a soundtrack by Jeff Ensign. Anthropomorphic, identity-less figures overrun a fortress in a spaceless, timeless landscape. The film is part of a multidisciplinary project that also includes a photographic series and mixed-technique paintings; it won the Golden Nica for Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2011.

title: MetaPhase: a contrapuntal dialogue between a pianist and her avatar in the metaverse
media: Performance / body | VR / AR / XR | Sensor / interaction
summary: MetaPhase is an XR piano performance by pianist and researcher Giusy Caruso with the Milan company LWT3, presented at Cremona Musica on 23 September 2022. Wearing a suit with light-reflecting markers, an sEMG biosensor and an Oculus Rift headset, Caruso plays the counterpoint part of Steve Reich's Piano Phase with an avatar pianist animated from her own previously recorded movements and Yamaha Disklavier audio, while her biosignals modify visuals, video effects and audio parameters. The audience watches the virtual scene projected in real time, can choose viewpoints and view the data, and could afterwards experience the performance in VR; it received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2023.

title: Micro-Nano Landscape
summary: A video work built from high-magnification microscope recordings of magnetically controlled micro-nano robotic collectives: magnetic microparticles that, under a dual-axis oscillating magnetic field, self-assemble into clusters, grow, tilt and move together. The footage, which the catalogue states is not animated or simulated, is enlarged to projection scale and presented as landscape- and calligraphy-like imagery. Made by Suxuan Jiang with research collaboration from Jiangfan Yu and support from the Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society (AIRS) SciArt Co-lab; Honorary Mention, New Animation Art, Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Mid Tide #3
summary: A silent three-channel video installation (48:49 seamless loop) made from three and a half hours of fixed-camera 4K 120fps footage of waves breaking against rocks as the light and tide change. Furusawa's own software turns the footage into a 3D object with time as its depth and cuts it along freely moving planes instead of the usual front-to-back playback, so different moments appear side by side within one frame. Viewers watch the waves keep their form while the rocks appear to metamorphose.

title: Midéegaadi
media: Screen / monitor | Performance / body | Material / sculpture
summary: Midéegaadi is a series of videos in which Cannupa Hanska Luger wears bison regalia made from repurposed materials and dances to call bison back onto the land, enacting a Northern Plains ancestral practice. In April 2025 it was shown as a multi-channel presentation on more than 92 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight as a Midnight Moment commission with For Freedoms, with a live performance by Mali Obomsawin and Deerlady on 11 April. It is part of the artist's ongoing speculative fiction project Future Ancestral Technologies.

title: Mindscapes (series, Kinect installation)
summary: Part of the Mindscapes series (begun 2010), in which the artist explores the idea of landscape in relation to brain activity using custom programming algorithms. In the 2012 solo show at Zipper Galeria, São Paulo, the darkened main room held an interactive installation where a 3D object formed in real time from ambient sound, while a Kinect infrared sensor mapped visitors' movements; projections covered a wall of about 30×65 feet. A neon piece reading "saudade" was shown in a transitional space, its lights vibrating at different frequencies that visitors could change with a dimmer.

title: Mnemosyne
summary: A 35-minute immersive work that combines VR film (360° animation and 180° live-action footage) with live theatre performance and an installation environment of meditation booths, inspired by Tang Xianzu's Ming Dynasty play The Peony Pavilion. Audience members wear headsets inside the installation and, near the end, meet a live actor with mixed reality elements. It was shown in the Future Cinema section of the Shanghai International Film Festival (2025) and out of competition in the Biennale College Cinema – Immersive section of Venice Immersive 2025.

title: Momentum
summary: Momentum is an installation of light, sound and movement commissioned by the Barbican Centre for its 90-metre-long Curve gallery in London, shown from 13 February to 1 June 2014. Visitors walk at their own pace through a darkened space in which 12 software-controlled pendulums with changing white lamps swing on two axes, sometimes stopping mid-swing, and project shadows and planes of light across the walls and curved floor, accompanied by a soundtrack.

title: MOON GOOSE ANALOGUE: Lunar Migration Bird Facility
media: Performance / body | Screen / monitor | Network / data
summary: The Moon Goose Analogue: Lunar Migration Bird Facility builds on Francis Godwin's 17th-century story The Man in the Moone, in which a man flies to the Moon in a chariot towed by 'moon geese'. The artist raised eleven geese from birth at Pollinaria in Italy, gave them astronauts' names, imprinted them on herself as goose-mother, trained them to fly and housed them in a remote Moon analogue habitat. In the gallery, visitors meet a control-room installation with consoles, a live stream from the habitat, instructional videos, photographs and vitrines of the geese's egg shells and footprints.

title: Mosaic Virus
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Mosaic Virus is a GAN-generated video of tulips whose appearance changes with the price of bitcoin: the generated petals show more stripes as the price rises and a single colour as it falls. The model was trained on a dataset of about ten thousand tulip photographs the artist took and categorised by hand. The 2018 version is a single-screen work showing a grid of tulips (commissioned by Impakt within EMAP/EMARE); a 2019 version is a three-screen installation.

title: Mother Courage
summary: Mother Courage is an installation in a white Kombi camper van that houses a dual-screen projection of an elderly Aboriginal woman artist, played by artist Grace Rubuntja, painting dot paintings among paint pots, utensils and bedding, while her grandson sits listening to Aboriginal rock music on a radio in the van. Visitors look in through the van's windows and rear doors. Commissioned by dOCUMENTA (13) and ACMI, it was first shown at dOCUMENTA (13) in Kassel in 2012, where the van was moved around the city and parked at different sites, and then installed in a gallery at ACMI, Melbourne, in 2013.

title: Mourning Class: Nollywood
summary: Mourning Class: Nollywood is a video installation, the first in Saro-Wiwa's Mourning Class series of video performances about mourning rituals. Nigerian actresses sit in close-up before the camera, shoulders bare and heads covered, and cry real tears when prompted by the artist; Wikipedia adds that each breaks the performance with a smile. It was first presented in 2010 in Sharon Stone in Abuja, an exhibition on Nollywood that Saro-Wiwa co-curated at Location One gallery in New York, and has been shown as both a single-channel and a multi-channel work.

title: Moving Earth, Crossing Water, Eating Soil
summary: A multipart mixed-media installation on St John's Island (Pulau Sekijang Bendera), Singapore, commissioned for Singapore Biennale 2022 (Natasha), with performances and activations. In the island's main administrative building a four-pillared structure based on the Javanese saka guru holds a shrine-like arrangement of objects referring to the island's history, with painted cutouts of eight animals from Bugis divination diagrams; visitors follow nine archetypal symbols (The Guide, The Witness, The Wrathful Deity and others). In the garden, eight wind-driven wooden instruments strike bamboo plates, and visitors can also turn them by hand.

title: Moving Parts
summary: A sound and video exhibition built from field recordings and footage made on Lagos bridges, especially pedestrian bridges, installed across multiple screens in Odeya Carpark, Onikan, Lagos Island, in November 2025. Visitors move through the audio-visual installation; on the opening day the artist performed the score live with double bass, percussion and flutes.

title: Music of the Spheres
summary: Música de las esferas (Music of the Spheres) is an installation shown in the Cuban Pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale in 2013: a glass sphere suspended from the ceiling containing a motor-driven music box, with a light box. An empty circular musical staff was laid over an image of the solar system and a note assigned wherever a planet fell; the music box plays the resulting 30-second looped composition of nine notes.

title: Máquina Stella
summary: Máquina Stella is an electromechanical sculpture made of aluminium, Teflon, resistive filaments, electricity, a mechanical system and electronic control, built as a dodecahedron with twelve limbs. Along each limb an electromechanical terminal moves lengthwise to energise a metal filament that glows red hot, in a programme that distributes the available energy between the parts. It received the ARCO/BEEP Electronic Art Award at ARCO Madrid in February 2012.

title: Máquinas Salvajes
media: Robotics / kinetics | Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction
summary: Máquinas Salvajes (Wild Machines) consists of biodegradable mechanical sculptures with wooden skeletons and biopolymer skins (agar-agar and gelatin) made from materials of Costa Rican ecosystems. Two were left in the Sarapiquí rainforest and in Orotina to decay or be eaten, which was documented on video; in the exhibition (Lentos Museum, Linz, 2023) the videos are shown with a third sculpture that a sensor sprays with water when visitors are present, gradually degrading it. The project received a 2023 CIFO-Ars Electronica Award.

title: Nairobi Berries
summary: A 360-degree virtual reality film for mobile VR that combines live-action footage of Nairobi with animation and a lyrical voice-over by Mukii; its synopsis describes two women and a man who wrangle in forests full of smoke and beneath still waters. The viewer, wearing a headset, is moved through city locations with vertical camera movements, into the ground and up from under water, ending at night under water. It was made with Electric South's New Dimensions grant and won the first Immersive Encounters Grand Prix at Encounters Film Festival in 2017.

title: Nanohana Heels - Healing Fukushima
summary: A pair of mechanical high-heeled shoes that plant rapeseed (nanohana) into the soil as the wearer walks, made by Sputniko! in collaboration with shoe designer Masaya Kushino. The project refers to experiments in which rapeseed absorbed caesium and strontium from contaminated soil after Chernobyl and to rapeseed-planting initiatives in Fukushima after the 2011 nuclear accident. It received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: Necomimi
summary: Necomimi is a headband with motorised cat ears driven by a brainwave sensor: the ears rise when the wearer is concentrating, lie down when the wearer is relaxed, and rise and move when both happen at once. It was developed by the neurowear project team at Dentsu, first shown as a prototype at an event in Omotesando, Tokyo, and later manufactured and sold by NeuroSky. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: Neo Geo City
summary: Neo Geo City is a website at its own domain (neogeocity.com), supported by ZKM Karlsruhe and coded by Reinier Feijen, showing an abstract city of large, variously coloured cubes. According to ZKM, visitors fly over the city, can grab and move the cubes in any direction with the mouse, and clicking one turns the scene black so that only wire-frame models remain; the city extends endlessly in whichever direction is chosen.

title: Never real historians, always near poets
summary: A video projection installation commissioned for Singapore Biennale 2019 and shown at National Gallery Singapore. It centres on members of Phaophanit's family who made different decisions after the 1975 regime change in Laos, some leaving for France and others staying, with footage and interviews filmed in Savannakhet, Laos, and in St. Denis near Paris. The soundscape was composed by the artists' son, Savanh.

title: Night Charades
summary: Night Charades is a silent AI-generated animation commissioned for the LED facade of the M+ museum in Hong Kong, shown nightly from 22 March to 29 June 2025. Animated characters mime around 50 scenes, gestures and poses from 1980s and 1990s Hong Kong cinema, re-enacting roles originally played by actors such as Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung and Chow Yun-fat. An algorithm continuously reshuffles the scenes and characters into new combinations, viewed by passers-by across Victoria Harbour.

title: No Bird
media: Robotics / kinetics | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: A kinetic installation (265 x 265 x 150 cm) on a sand surface with two machines: a bird-like walking machine that leaves bird footprints in the sand, and a trace-erasing machine following behind that scratches out the tracks with a toothbrush, smooths them with a wire rake and flattens the surface with soft bristles. According to designboom, the movement is triggered by a sensor when a viewer comes close and runs for about two minutes while the viewer stays in range. The duo (Yoo Byoung-Joon and Lim Hee-Young, Seoul) received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Norman
media: VR / AR / XR | Online / net art
summary: Norman is an open-source animation tool written in JavaScript that runs in a web browser and lets the user draw frame-by-frame animation in 3D space with VR controllers. One mode creates a new frame and advances the timeline each time the user makes a mark. The tool was made with support from Google Creative Lab, and its animations could also be viewed in a browser.

title: NoSearchBar
summary: NoSearchBar is a Chrome browser extension that removes the search bar from every website, including search engines such as google.com, and changes the browser's search provider so that searching from the URL address bar is disabled. A user who installs it can only reach content through what websites offer without a search, such as categories, sorting, forecasts and recommendation systems. It was made in the New Media Class at UdK Berlin (winter 2021) and received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art+ at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: Not Your World Music: Noise in South East Asia
summary: Not Your World Music: Noise in South East Asia is a 276-page book with a companion CD compilation on noise, electroacoustic, industrial and experimental music and sound art in Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. It contains historical, political and sociological essays, interviews with artists and organisers, a bibliography of popular music from the region and a discography; the compilation features exclusive tracks by twelve artists from the region. It was published in September 2016 by Syrphe (Berlin) and Hushush (Ottawa) under a Creative Commons licence and is also available as a free PDF.

title: Nothing to See Here
media: Camera / computer vision | Sound | Sensor / interaction
summary: Nothing to See Here is an interactive viewing box by Celine Daemen and Studio Nergens, installed in public spaces such as train stations. A visitor looks through stereoscopic spyholes in a mirrored cube and sees a live 3D image of themselves from above, peering into the box, while fictional figures (a confused man, a wolf, a plastic bag) and a spatial soundscape act around this double. A prototype was shown at Cultura Nova in Heerlen station in 2025 and the world premiere was at IDFA DocLab in November 2025.

title: Now he's out in public and everyone can see
media: Screen / monitor | Online / net art | Sound
summary: Now he's out in public and everyone can see is an 18-channel video installation in which 18 monitors of different sizes hang on cables at varying heights around a darkened room. A 16-minute narrative edits together excerpts from hundreds of YouTube vlogs in which people comment on viral media scandals involving four famous African American men, whose names are removed so that the speakers seem to discuss one unnamed man; voices sometimes speak in unison and sometimes answer or contradict each other. Visitors move around the room to follow speakers who are never all in view at once. It premiered at LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions) in 2012 and was remade as a single-channel film in 2017.

title: Now You See Me, Now You Don't
summary: An installation of 12 trampolines set flush into a desert valley near AlUla to resemble puddles, commissioned for the first Desert X AlUla (2020) and since on permanent display. Visitors can touch, lie on and jump on them; after dark the trampolines are lit and change in appearance as people interact with them. The work addresses water scarcity in Saudi Arabia.

title: Nuestra Victoria (Our Victory)
media: Camera / computer vision | Screen / monitor | Online / net art
summary: A series of works built on a 3D digital archive of Mexico City's Angel of Independence monument. Gil documented the monument with drone footage and photogrammetry after feminist protests against violence towards women in August 2019, before it was boarded up and restored. The record is shown as video (in one installation on two 55-inch screens, commissioned for Storefront TV) and as photographic prints, and the 3D files can be downloaded.

title: Nuit Blanche
artist: Arev Manoukian, Marc-André Gray (National Film Board of Canada)
summary: Nuit Blanche is a black-and-white short film of about four minutes, directed by Arev Manoukian with visual effects by Marc-André Gray, set on a 1950s cobblestone street where a man looks at a woman in a café across the street. Live action shot at up to 2,000 frames per second is combined with 3-D effects and matte paintings, so the moment of attraction between the two strangers is stretched into slow motion as glass and water burst around them. It received the Golden Nica for Computer Animation / Film / VFX at Prix Ars Electronica 2010.

title: Nyctinasty
summary: A black-and-white single-channel film of about 7 minutes 54 seconds in which the artist, as protagonist, carries out an evening routine of cleansing and self-care alone in a modernist house before nightfall, as unseen presences gather. It borrows the pacing of horror cinema and draws on Aboriginal practices of caring for body and spirit after death. It was commissioned by the National Gallery of Australia for the 4th National Indigenous Art Triennial: Ceremony (2022).

title: O Século (The Century)
summary: A video of about nine and a half minutes (MASP lists 9'37") with a fixed view of a street. It begins with only the sound of people running; then objects of every sort are thrown into the frame until the street is filled with debris, dust and smoke, while the people involved stay out of view.

title: Occupy George
summary: Occupy George is a set of rubber stamps that print infographics on US one-dollar bills, showing statistics on wealth and income disparity in America, such as how much wealth the richest 400 Americans hold or the ratio of CEO to worker pay. Ivan Cash and Andy Dao stamped bills and exchanged them for unmarked ones at Occupy Wall Street protests, so the marked bills circulated as ordinary money; templates were offered online for people to print their own. The project was later shown at Ars Electronica (Honorary Mention, Interactive Art, 2012) and entered the V&A collection, which commissioned a version for the UK £5 note.

title: Oceans in Transformation
summary: Oceans in Transformation is a three-year research project by Territorial Agency (John Palmesino and Ann-Sofi Rönnskog), commissioned by TBA21–Academy, that assembles satellite remote-sensing, bathymetric, fishing, shipping and climate data into large dynamic image compositions of the changing world ocean. It was shown as an exhibition at Ocean Space, Church of San Lorenzo, Venice (2020–2021), released online in seven trajectories on Ocean Archive with essays co-edited with e-flux Architecture, and accompanied by 'Messy Studio' gatherings with scientists, activists and policymakers. It won the S+T+ARTS Prize 2021 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration.

title: Octopocalypse
summary: Octopocalypse is an immersive installation for three participants, who enter an interrogation room after a fictional meteor storm and face an alien octopus that communicates through music, touch, rhythm and visions. With questions, button presses and rhythm the group shapes the outcome and builds a music track from impulses sent by the alien, choosing whether to interrogate it or earn its trust. It premiered in the Venice Immersive competition in 2026; the makers say they used generative AI as a production tool.

title: Octopus
summary: Octopus is a multichannel video installation (four synchronized projections, about 18:30 minutes, shown with Home Depot buckets) produced during the artist's residency at the Hammer Museum, Los Angeles. It shows a dozen Guatemalan Mayan immigrants, day laborers who fought in the Guatemalan civil war, some on both sides, reenacting that war in the parking lot of a Home Depot store in Los Angeles where they wait to be hired. The title refers to the Guatemalan nickname for the United Fruit Company.

title: Octópodos Sisíficos
summary: Octópodos Sisíficos (Sisyphean Octopods) is an installation of six mobile robots developed by the Artes Electrónicas group at the Universidad Nacional de Tres de Febrero, Argentina, directed by Mariela Yeregui, with robotic design by Miguel Grassi. Each robot carries an LCD screen showing endoscopic video images that resemble internal body organs and moves on an erratic course; the robots have no self-positioning or navigation mechanism and each is attached to the wall by a flexible corrugated metal tube.

title: Odiolândia (Hateland)
media: Screen / monitor | Text / print | Network / data
summary: A video without images that shows comments posted on social media about the São Paulo city and state governments' operations in Cracolândia between 21 May and 9 June 2017. The audio comes from videos that participants in those operations posted online. The comments are shown as posted, without grammatical or stylistic corrections; the artist removed only electoral content. It was made for the exhibition São Paulo não é uma cidade: as invenções do centro at Sesc 24 de Maio, São Paulo.

title: Of Men and Gods and Mud
summary: A three-channel video installation shown at the 59th Venice Biennale (The Milk of Dreams), where Cherri received the Silver Lion for a Promising Young Participant. Shot mainly at a brickyard near the Merowe Dam on the Nile in northern Sudan, it follows a seasonal brickmaker who shapes mud into bricks by day and at night secretly builds a structure of mud and scrap that becomes a creature. It was shown alongside drawings of mud creatures and three sculptural figures, Titans.

title: Oikeiōsis
summary: Oikeiōsis is a two-room installation by Pavlina Vagioni at Spazio Tana, Venice, presented by the Hellenic Diaspora Foundation during the 61st Biennale Arte (6 May - 25 October 2026). In the first room, Neikos, a polygonal plexiglass cube reflects visitors in fragmented form; in the second, Philotes, six rock-salt seats surround a hexagonal mirrored structure, and when visitors sit, sound and light respond, building a layered vocal soundscape that includes the artist's soprano voice. The salt seats change shape over the exhibition through visitors' touch.

title: On a Clear Day You Can See Forever
summary: A two-channel video installation (synchronised rear HD projections, colour, four-channel sound, 39 min) on translucent voile screens held in a parallel, trapezoid frame, shown in a shop unit at Lucky Plaza, Orchard Road, for Singapore Biennale 2025. One screen shows Inuka, Singapore's first polar bear born in captivity, circling in his zoo enclosure; the other shows 80km/h (2004), a single-take drive along the Pan Island Expressway filmed from the passenger seat at a constant 80 km/h. Visitors view the two projections overlapping through the frame.

title: Once Upon a Garden
summary: An ongoing series (begun 2021, first shown as a special project commissioned by ART X Lagos in 2022) in which the artist trained a GAN, and later diffusion and video models, on records of extinct and critically endangered flora from the Sahel region of West Africa to generate images of these plants. In the first chapter the generated flowers were curated, animated and composited into artificial gardens installed at exhibitions; the complete series (2022–2024) presents 50 speculative flora across five chapters.

title: Ongoing, Individual Adaptability or How to Quiet Quit
summary: A two-part web work commissioned for the Whitney Museum's artport, made with a generative adversarial network (GAN) trained on thousands of installation photographs of Whitney exhibitions. The first part, Ongoing, Individual Adaptability, shows twelve GAN images collaged with manipulated excerpts of artist correspondence and ephemera from the Whitney's library; the second, How to Quiet Quit, is three videos of the GAN producing images, with soundtracks of TED-talk excerpts by Nick Bostrom, Kai-Fu Lee and Janelle Shane interrupted by the artist's comments and questions. Visitors change the sequence of images and videos by refreshing the page; the title quotes Octavia E. Butler's Parable of the Sower.

title: Open Source Estrogen
media: Material / sculpture | Performance / body | Screen / monitor
summary: Open Source Estrogen is a collaborative research project by Mary Maggic, begun with Byron Rich, that combines biohacking and speculative design around the hormone estrogen, aiming to develop do-it-yourself / do-it-with-others protocols for detecting and extracting it. Its protocols include transgenic yeast sensors for estrogenic compounds, DIY column chromatography with cigarette filters, silica gel and methanol to extract hormones from urine, and solid-phase extraction of estrogenic compounds from water; it is carried out through public workshops, kitchen performance and videos such as Housewives Making Drugs. It received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2017.

title: OpenSurgery - A do-it-yourself surgery robot for domestic laparoscopy
summary: OpenSurgery is a do-it-yourself robot-assisted surgery system for keyhole (laparoscopic) surgery at home, built from 3D-printed and laser-cut parts, hacked surgical instruments and components bought online, with electronics taken from 3D-printer designs, for about $5,000. The prototype moves but is not stable enough for surgery; at the exhibition it ran through a randomised series of movements. It was developed as a graduation project at the Design Interactions department of the Royal College of Art, London, in 2015.

title: OPERA
summary: An 8K animation conceived as an installation: a looping cycle of about five minutes showing a giant pyramid filled with hundreds of small black-and-white figures in a hierarchical society, passing through day and night, modelled on Renaissance fresco murals. The installation version has no dialogue and no camera movement; visitors walk along the image and choose which characters and sections to follow. A cinema version was nominated for the 2021 Academy Award for Animated Short Film, and the work received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Our Islands 11°16’58.4”N 123°45’07.0”E
summary: A video in which underwater compressor divers from Bantayan Island, Philippines, stage a version of the annual Ati-Atihan parade on the floor of the Visayan Sea, wearing costumes that reference religious, animistic and pop culture figures. The coordinates in the title were chosen by the divers according to tide, current and time of day. It was shown in the Statements sector of Art Basel 2017 with Silverlens and screened nightly on Times Square billboards in July 2024 as part of Midnight Moment.

title: Pandemonium
media: Projection | VR / AR / XR | Robotics / kinetics
summary: A multimedia project that premiered in October 2025 at Moore College of Art & Design and the Fels Planetarium at The Franklin Institute, Philadelphia. It combines mechatronics, animation and sound with a 360-degree film shown with 8K projection in the planetarium dome, and the opening performance used a robot. The film shows a tornado of debris, including newspaper clippings swirling out of a tornado machine built by the artist; at the 2026 Whitney Biennial it was shown on a 20-ft circular screen overhead (approx. 20 min.).

title: Paper Tears
summary: An installation of light, sound, choreography and image for Catalonia in Venice, a collateral event of the 61st Venice Biennale (Docks Cantieri Cucchini, 9 May–22 November 2026), curated by Elise Lammer for the Institut Ramon Llull. Four lasers project 15th-century paper watermarks from the archive of the Museu Molí Paperer de Capellades, a sculptural LED screen shows drone footage of four aquifer springs, and performers dressed as jesters deliver monologues in a script structured like a waltz, with a soundtrack. Visitors walk around and onto platforms to change their point of view.

title: Parasitic / Symbiotic
media: Robotics / kinetics | Material / sculpture | Text / print
summary: A technical device mounted on a living tree in a forest contains a milling machine that moves along the trunk and carves an encoded version of Joseph von Eichendorff's Romantic poem "Abschied" into the bark. The carving remains on the tree, which continues to grow around it. The work was Krenz's master thesis at the University of the Arts Berlin and received an Award of Distinction in Interactive Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2016.

title: Phantom Ride
summary: Phantom Ride is a two-channel video installation by Daniel Crooks, made as the second Ian Potter Moving Image Commission and shown at ACMI, Melbourne (16 February – 29 May 2016); it is in the ACMI collection. Footage of tracks in urban and country settings (tram tracks, tram repair depots, bridges and tunnels along disused railways), shot with a computerised dolly, is stitched into what appears to be a single continuous journey referencing the 'phantom rides' of early cinema. It is projected on a double-sided screen: one side shows the journey travelling forward, the other the view travelling backward.

title: Pinktoned (Exploded View)
summary: A multi-screen installation shown in its own room at the Hammer Museum's Made in L.A. 2025. It presents the component parts of Stoltz's 16mm film Pinktoned separately: footage of passersby filmed from his East Hollywood studio, faded 1976 slides of Los Angeles streets wheat-pasted with posters for the documentary Underground, and a black-and-white moving graphic. A third screen runs a 16mm optical soundtrack of 'pink tone' test frequencies on a loop, and visitors see the street footage and the slides across the room from each other.

title: Pixel Dust
summary: Pixel Dust is a video of pulsating particles made with the artist's custom software, premiered as Times Square Arts' Midnight Moment for November 2025. It played synchronized on over 90 electronic billboards in Times Square nightly from 11:57pm to midnight, November 1-30, 2025.

title: PL'AI
media: Robotics / kinetics | AI / generative | Camera / computer vision
summary: An installation lasting several months in which cucumber plants grown from seed and an AI-controlled robot about three metres tall interact. The robot moves 36 bouncy balls on stainless steel threads above a tray of plants; a camera and a 3D scanner (scanning every 15 minutes) feed the AI, and when a plant's tendril grabs a ball, that ball stops moving. Produced in 2020 by Kersnikova Institute / Kapelica Gallery (European ARTificial Intelligence Lab), it received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: plain voices
summary: plain voices (Que voz feio) is an eight-minute two-channel video in which twin sisters, filmed in separate places, each recount in Portuguese the same incident from their early childhood, with subtitles. Shown on two screens at once, the two accounts differ slightly, and following one image, voice and subtitle means missing the other. It was shown at the Image Forum Festival 2011 and won the Grand Prize in the 15th Japan Media Arts Festival Art Division.

title: Plan B
summary: Plan B was the Pavilion of Turkey at the 54th Venice Biennale (Artiglierie, Arsenale, 4 June–27 November 2011), curated by Fulya Erdemci: a working water-purification unit whose components were separated and spread through a room with a window onto the canal, reconnected by extended pipes painted in colours according to their function. Canal water was piped in, desalinated and purified to drinking quality, and returned to the canal; visitors stood among the machines and their noise while the water itself stayed out of sight inside the pipes.

title: Pocket Money
summary: Pocket Money is a video work of about 15 minutes, shot between September and December 2025, featuring about 20 young people from in and around Adelaide in their first paid jobs, such as fast food and shelf-stacking, as well as at rest in their bedrooms, spending money and pursuing hobbies. It was shown in the 2026 Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art: Yield Strength (27 February – 8 June 2026).

title: Pollinator Pathmaker
media: AI / generative | Online / net art | Material / sculpture
summary: An algorithmic garden-design tool and website (pollinator.art) that generates planting designs computed to support the greatest number of pollinator species, choosing from curated regional plant palettes. Users select their garden conditions, receive a unique design they can explore in 3D or with a 'pollinator vision' view, and download planting instructions with an edition certificate; each planted garden is an edition of the work. Commissioned Editions have been planted at the Eden Project, Cornwall (2022), for the Serpentine in Kensington Gardens, London, and outside the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin (LAS Art Foundation); it won the S+T+ARTS Grand Prize 2023.

title: Prometheus Firebringer
summary: Prometheus Firebringer is a lecture-performance of about an hour on generative AI, technology and power. On one side of the stage, a chorus of AI-generated Greek masks with AI-generated voices performs a new version each night of the lost final play of Aeschylus' Prometheia trilogy, generated by a GPT language model; on the other side, Dorsen delivers a talk composed entirely of passages quoted from other texts. It premiered at Bryn Mawr College in January 2023 and was then presented at The Chocolate Factory, Theatre for a New Audience and REDCAT.

title: Protei
summary: Protei is an open-hardware, shape-shifting sailing robot: an unmanned sailboat whose whole hull bends to steer it, developed so it can sail against the wind and tow oil-absorbent material to intercept drifting oil spills. The designs are published under an open-hardware licence so others can build, modify and share improvements; later uses proposed include measuring radioactivity and plastic debris and monitoring fisheries and coral reefs. It received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2012, where it was described as still under construction.

title: puberty
summary: puberty is an installation commissioned for the Simon Lee Foundation Institute of Contemporary Asian Art at the Art Gallery of Western Australia, shown in the gallery foyer from 22 July to 11 December 2022. It combines animation on an iPad with cast acrylic, chain, fans and synthetic turf, forming a face whose eyes, nose, tongue and mouth are described by the venue as moving elements.

title: Quando o segundo Sol chegar / Um cometa nos teus olhos
summary: A two-channel video installation, the third film of a trilogy made on the Transamazônica highway (BR-230), shown in MASP's Video Room. It shows scenes of the highway under a fleeting glow that suggests a 'second Sun' approaching Earth, set against a text that tells a physical and existential journey. The project began during a residency at the Centro Cultural do Cariri awarded at the 22nd Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil.

title: Quine
media: AI / generative | Network / data | Text / print
summary: Quine is a generative series of 497 blockchain-based artworks by Larva Labs (Matt Hall and John Watkinson), released on October 9, 2025 as the final Art Blocks Curated project. Each work's image contains the source code of the program that generates it, laid out on a grid; some outputs reproduce themselves exactly while others cycle through several generations, and collectors can choose which generation to display. At Zero 10, Art Basel Miami Beach 2025, all 497 works were shown in miniature on a vitrine table, with 10 shown as signed, framed works.

title: RADIO GHOST
summary: Radio Ghost is an audio-driven, app-based walking game for three players set in a shopping centre, part game, part interactive radio show and part ghost hunt. Players act as ghost hunters, following audio prompts on phones and blending in as shoppers to unlock stories of the mall connected to the supply chains of the goods on sale. It was commissioned by LIFT Festival 2022 and won the Lumen Prize Interactive Award 2022.

title: Raster und Spectrum
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Raster und Spectrum is an onchain abstract real-time animation that can play on any device, shown by Nguyen Wahed in the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach 2025. Two brushes — a raster of white lines on black and a spectrum that continuously cycles through hues — cross the screen in one of eight directions and return when they meet an edge.

title: Re: cite, member, sist
summary: Re: cite, member, sist is a site-specific installation with textile, 4-channel sound and found material, commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances) and shown at Colpetty Town House, Colombo. According to the festival publication it combines layered cyanotypes, shadow drawings referencing early illustrations of Portuguese colonial exploits, tracings of the artist's grandmother's embroidery patterns on cushions, curtains and household objects, and sound recordings of ocean tides and dialogues with her aunt. It draws on the artist's family's Goan history and her grandmother's migration from Bardez to Karachi.

title: Real-time AR visual show for Nosaj Thing
media: Camera / computer vision | Performance / body | Sound
summary: A touring live audiovisual show by Daito Manabe (Rhizomatiks) and the musician Nosaj Thing (Jason Chung), developed from a 2015 prototype for Taico Club in Japan and presented at Coachella 2016 and at Sónar festivals. Kinect depth cameras around the stage, a motion-capture suit and head camera worn by Nosaj Thing, and a camera operator moving on stage feed a system that renders the performers as 3-D figures in real time, synchronised with MIDI and audio from his laptop. The audience sees the two performers on stage and, on the screens, a computer-generated version of the same scene from changing camera viewpoints.

title: Reality Looks Back
summary: A 21-minute dome documentary, world-premiered in the IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction in 2025 and shown in the DocLab Exhibition and at the Planetarium, directed by Anne Jeppesen with co-director Omid Zarei (Superposition XR Studio). Jeppesen's narration moves through quantum observation, split déjà vu, parallel realities and the death of her elderly hamster Oliver, over documentary footage processed into Gaussian splats. The work began as an audio piece made in the YASS! mentorship programme (Lucia Festival / Radio Papesse), premiered in Florence in 2024.

title: Regular Animals
media: Robotics / kinetics | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Regular Animals is an installation of autonomous robot dogs fitted with hyper-realistic silicone heads of figures including Andy Warhol, Pablo Picasso, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Beeple himself, which move around a glass-walled pen using LIDAR to avoid each other. The robots take pictures of their surroundings, reinterpret them with AI in the style associated with each character, and print them out of their rear; some of the prints carry QR codes to claim NFTs. It was first shown at Art Basel Miami Beach's Zero 10 section in December 2025 and later at the Neue Nationalgalerie, Berlin, in 2026.

title: Reifying Desire
summary: A series of six videos (2011–14) in which Satterwhite performs in front of a green screen and composites his performances into 3D-animated environments built from tracings of his mother Patricia's drawings of invented consumer objects. Later chapters add footage of other performers and public sites; the sixth chapter was shown in the 2014 Whitney Biennial.

title: REPETAE
summary: A series of language artworks combining AI-generated text, code-based visuals sketched in p5.js, and digitally looped and layered spoken word, presented as standalone works and longer interconnected cycles built around repetition. Parts include a browser-based piece that generates a new line of poetry every few minutes from the mantra WORDS CAN COMMUNICATE BEYOND WORDS. It received a Prix Ars Electronica 2024 Award of Distinction (AI in ART) and was shown as REPETAE: Again, Again at the Lentos Museum, Linz.

title: Requiem for an Exit
summary: An installation centred on a four-metre-tall armless robotic figure on a steel and hydraulic structure, whose hyperrealistic face is a projected animation built from a motion-capture recording of Thomas Kvam. In a darkened room with multichannel sound, the robot delivers a monologue written by the artists and voiced with AI speech synthesis, tracing genocide through human history from the disappearance of the Neanderthals; there is no interactivity. First shown at Meta.Morf 2024 in Trondheim (co-produced by TEKS); Golden Nica, New Animation Art, Prix Ars Electronica 2025.

title: Resonance Study IV
summary: Resonance Study IV is a multimedia digital sound installation (7 minutes 10 seconds, looped) by Colombo-based audio/visual artist Asvajit Boyle, shown at the first Lahore Biennale (LB01) in 2018. According to the Biennale, Boyle used an image-based sound editor, synthesizer and processor together with Google's Deep Dream computer-vision program to turn sounds into images and images into sound. Visitors meet the resulting images and soundscape as an audio-visual installation.

title: rheo: 5 horizons
summary: rheo: 5 horizons is an audiovisual installation of five vertical flat-panel displays and five speakers set in a row, each display paired and synchronised with its own mono sound channel. Video and field recordings of real landscapes are transformed by digital processing into graphic analyses and re-syntheses, so that the movement of the images indicates the position and direction of the sounds. It received the Golden Nica in the Digital Musics & Sound Art category of the Prix Ars Electronica 2010.

title: Rhythmic Ramp
summary: Rhythmic Ramp (Rampa rítmica) is a site-specific work by Cevdet Erek on the external ramp of Oscar Niemeyer's Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, the ramp that connects the exhibition's floors. It combines sonic and geometric elements placed along the ramp. Its sound includes rhythmic patterns drawn from music undergrounds in Istanbul and from São Paulo's vernacular rhythms, and visitors and passersby meet it as they go up and down the ramp.

title: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio (Re-launching Luigi Broglio)
summary: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio is a 33-minute 360° VR film directed by Vincenzo Cavallo, staged like a theatre piece, about Luigi Broglio, who launched Italy into space from the San Marco sea platform off Kenya in the 1960s. The viewer watches a confrontation between Broglio and a journalist in the abandoned command centre, with flashbacks to the African expedition, an encounter with Enrico Mattei and a near-diplomatic crisis with President Nasser. It was supported by Biennale College Cinema Immersive and shown out of competition at Venice Immersive 2025.

title: Riccardo Uncut
summary: Riccardo Uncut is an online work commissioned by the Whitney Museum's artport: the artists posted a call on social media offering to buy someone's phone for $1,000 and turned its photo and video contents into a customized, chronological slideshow. Viewers see roughly three thousand images taken between 2004 and 2017 by the chosen applicant, Riccardo — travels, friends and family, partners, home and office life, food and art. The accompanying song, from the soundtrack of Fassbinder's film Querelle (1982), also appears in one of Riccardo's videos.

title: Roz o shab (day and night)
summary: Roz o shab (day and night) is a site-specific neon installation made for the first Lahore Biennale (LB01, 2018) in the Summer Palace of the Lahore Fort. A maze of blue neon is threaded with red neon tracing the one route through it; its layout recalls the labyrinthine bhool bhulaiyan of Mughal architecture, and the Biennale relates the red and blue paths to verses by Muhammad Iqbal and to the cycle of night and day. According to Iftikhar Dadi, the work was shown for two weeks in March 2018 and destroyed after the Biennale ended.

title: Runnin'
media: VR / AR / XR | Performance / body | Sound
summary: Runnin' is an interactive VR music experience set to the track 'Runnin'' by Reggie Watts and John Tejada (Wajatta), made with volumetric capture of a cast of dancers at Intel Studios. The player starts in a neighbourhood record store and is transported to a retro-future dance party where dancers appear on the floor, walls and ceiling, and the player's actions trigger changes of perspective. It premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival New Frontier.

title: Résonances
summary: Résonances is an interactive installation in which a visitor's gestures return as a visual and sound echo: earlier actions resurface and overlap with present ones, so the visitor can choreograph the present on top of their own past. It was unveiled in December 2021 in the CORPS DATA exhibition at Îlot Balmoral in Montreal with ELEKTRA, and shown at the 6th International Digital Art Biennial (BIAN) at Arsenal Contemporary Art Montreal; an outdoor edition was presented at i Light Singapore 2023 and Future Media FEST 2024 in Taipei.

title: Sange Khara [Hard Stone]
summary: Sange Khara [Hard Stone] is an installation developed for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, anchored by a looping 16mm film of desert and oasis landscapes and figures drawn from cinematic references. Visitors sit or lie down under a tent-like canopy of melhifa cloth, a fabric worn by women in the Sahara, in a scenography based on nomadic structures of southern Morocco, surrounded by sound and light. It is a chapter of Hida's ongoing project Le Voyage du Phénix.

title: Satan in America and Other Invisible Evils: Experiments in Public Sculpture (Witches 1–3)
summary: Three witch figures in an installation shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026 that draws on scenes from American history, from the Salem witch trials to Abraham Lincoln's birth near Hodgenville, Kentucky. The witches' bodies are built from open-source medical 3D CT scans of human bodies, and two Salem villagers nearby are built from character models taken from the video game Doom. Visitors walk among figures mounted on metal poles alongside the artist's Symbolic Birth Cabin Unit and two demon figures.

title: Scanning
summary: Scanning is a single-channel video (41:56 mins) in which Amy Lee Sanford places, flips and scans, sheet by sheet, some 250 found letters on thin onion-skin paper. The letters were exchanged over five years between her adoptive mother in the United States and her biological father, who remained in Phnom Penh during the 1970–1975 civil war and the Khmer Rouge takeover in 1975. The work is in the Singapore Art Museum collection and was shown in Cinerama: Art and the Moving Image in Southeast Asia (SAM, 2017).

title: Screen Melancholy
media: Screen / monitor | Material / sculpture | AI / generative
summary: Screen Melancholy (2026) is a video installation by Li Yi-Fan, presented by the Taipei Fine Arts Museum as Taiwan's collateral event at the 61st Venice Biennale in the Palazzo delle Prigioni, curated by Raphael Fonseca. In the video, Li performs a monologue through a game-engine digital character in the tone of an online tutorial, addressing subscription-based image software and AI-generated images. Large sculptures of fragmented limbs are placed throughout the space; visitors can sit on them and charge their phones from chargers built into the sculptures.

title: SEA STATE
media: Screen / monitor | Material / sculpture | Text / print
