summary: A multi-part project begun in 2005 about Singapore's relationship to the sea, structured on the World Meteorological Organization's numbered sea-state scale. Its presentation at the Singapore Pavilion of the 56th Venice Biennale (2015) included a barnacle-covered buoy replica, archival material and maps, photographs, a large installation mapping Singapore's sea floor, and films on land reclamation and sand extraction.

title: SEFT-1 (Sonda de Exploración Ferroviaria Tripulada)
media: Robotics / kinetics | Network / data | Online / net art
summary: SEFT-1 (Manned Railway Exploration Probe) is a two-person vehicle built on the chassis of a convertible railway pickup truck, with an aluminium fuselage, that can travel on land or on rails; its makers, the 'ferronautas', drove it along Mexico's disused railway lines, guided by modern and 19th-century maps. On the way it records photographs, video, audio, text and interviews with people it meets, and transmits them to the project website, where its location, routes and recordings can be followed; in some towns the crew presents material gathered on earlier trips.

title: Shelter
summary: Shelter is a six-minute computer-animated short film with no dialogue. It begins in a fairly ordinary attic during a rainstorm, which becomes more and more surreal as the film goes on. Carl Burton made it with Cinema 4D and Adobe software, mostly during the month he takes off each year for personal work. It received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation/Film/VFX at Prix Ars Electronica 2013 and was screened at SIGGRAPH Asia 2012 and Slamdance 2013.

title: Skeleton of the Glorious
summary: Skeleton of the Glorious is a light installation by Khalid Zahid in the gardens of the King Abdulaziz Historical Center for Noor Riyadh 2025. It is a hollow, wireframe-like structure based on Al-Masmak Fort, the adobe and clay citadel of old Riyadh. It is lit from within, so the inner form is visible while the exterior falls into shadow.

title: Sky Brought Down
summary: A permanent site-specific sound installation in the atrium and main staircase of the Center for Imaging and Intervention at Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg. A weather station on the hospital roof sends real-time data (pressure, precipitation, wind, light) that software turns into sound textures, played through 16 speakers mounted behind floor-to-ceiling wooden panelling beneath a glass ceiling. People passing through the atrium hear the sky outside sonified along the vertical space; the work received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: SKY/WORLD DEATH/WORLD
media: Online / net art | Text / print | Screen / monitor
summary: A two-part Whitney artport commission for the Sunrise/Sunset series (Dec 2022–Apr 2023) that played on whitney.org at sunrise and sunset in New York. SKY/WORLD pairs game-engine animations of dawn, drawing on the Haudenosaunee story of Sky Woman, with the question "Who benefits from your burnout?"; DEATH/WORLD pairs abstract visuals and video of the artist recovered from the Internet Archive with "What is made bright by the loss of your light?". Viewers can click a switch to change the animation while answering text populates the screen.

title: SMOG SEASON
media: Sensor / interaction | Robotics / kinetics | Network / data
summary: SMOG SEASON is an installation of 80 cigarette packs mounted on 5 motor-driven circular bases, using Bangkok PM 2.5 air-pollution data and the cigarette-equivalence figure from Berkeley Earth (one cigarette per 22 micrograms per cubic meter per day). Visitors scan a QR code, choose a smoke level on their smartphone and hold it to a light sensor; the bases spin and lights blink at 18 FPS so the cigarette-label pictures appear animated, while an LED display shows the date, time and PM 2.5 value. It received an Honorary Mention in Prix Ars Electronica 2023 (New Animation Art).

title: Smoke and Mirrors
summary: A 4m30s data animation based on NASA's Blue Marble photograph: a counter shows atmospheric methane in parts per billion from 1970 to the present while the rotating globe fills with pink smoke, and advertising slogans from the oil industry (e.g. "Out to clean the air", "Unsettled Science", "Doomsday is cancelled") appear across the screen at their dates. It is set to the song "Oh My Heart" and was produced with the studio Parliament, using NOAA, NASA and EEA data. It received the Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica (New Animation Art) in 2024 and has been shown as a video and in exhibitions.

title: Soak
summary: Soak is an interactive installation in which an elastic spandex canvas glows in a dark room; when visitors touch, poke, rub or lean their whole body into it, the surface stretches and fills with colours spreading as if the cloth were absorbing dye. The colour is a simulated watercolour computed by GPU-accelerated cellular automata (built with Processing and Kinect, per the artists' site). It was a Jury Selection in the 15th Japan Media Arts Festival Art Division.

title: Soft Collision
media: Robotics / kinetics | Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction
summary: Soft Collision is a deformable pneumatic silicone membrane with embedded sensors that wraps a UR5 industrial robot arm. A person physically pushes and guides the arm to program its movement, then adjusts its trajectory through the sensors while it replays; air chambers inflate in short bursts as feedback. It was developed in the VOJEXT S+T+ARTS residency and shown with a performer.

title: Solwata
summary: Solwata is a 25-minute mixed reality installation, narrated by Mark Ruffalo, about rising seas and planned relocation in the Solomon Islands, co-produced by Human Rights Watch, Agog: The Immersive Media Institute and NowHere Media and shown in Venice Immersive 2026. Participants interact with water and artifacts and, through 360° video, Gaussian splats and 3D animation, join community members Martha, Francis and Lawrence. It was made with residents of Walande, Ngongosila and Kwai.

title: SONG 1
summary: SONG 1 was a video installation projected with 11 high-definition projectors onto the entire circular facade of the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden in Washington, D.C., from dusk to midnight between 22 March and 13 May 2012, forming a 360-degree image seen from the National Mall. On a loop, figures such as a businessman, a waitress, dancers and singers, including Tilda Swinton and John Doe, appear in diners, factories, cars and other everyday places, singing or moving to some 40 newly recorded versions of the song 'I Only Have Eyes for You'. The installation has no dialogue or fixed beginning and is meant to be come upon in passing.

title: Songs for dying
summary: A 30-minute HD film with installation, co-commissioned by the 13th Gwangju Biennale, Kunsthall Trondheim and the Han Nefkens Foundation, narrated by the voice of a sea turtle, that combines footage around the death and funeral of the artist's grandfather with Jeju Island's shamanic rituals commemorating the 1948 uprising and the 2020 pro-democracy protests in Thailand. In the installation the video is accompanied by a diorama figure of gravel, moss, clay, modelled roots and banana leaves, with hands cast from the grandfather's. It opened at Kunsthall Trondheim in February 2021 and was shown at the Gwangju Biennale the same year.

title: Sonic Inheritances
artist: Singing Wells (Ketebul Music and Abubilla Music)
summary: A listening space commissioned by Sharjah Art Foundation and Bergen Assembly, shown at Sharjah Biennial 16 (Bait Al Serkal, 6 February – 15 June 2025) and then at the fifth Bergen Assembly. It presents recordings, interviews and performance videos from Singing Wells' archive of East African music. Singing Wells was founded in 2011 by Nairobi's Ketebul Music and London's Abubilla Music, and travels to villages with a mobile recording studio.

title: Soundtrack
summary: Soundtrack is a color video with sound (11 min 12 sec) that takes eleven minutes of the soundtrack of Steven Spielberg's 2005 film War of the Worlds as a readymade and sets to it images shot in Ben-Ner's kitchen with his family. Ben-Ner and his two older children mouth the actors' lines while domestic actions such as blending a smoothie, swatting a fly, putting out a small kitchen fire or dropping a bottle of vodka follow the film's sound, intercut with internet footage from LiveLeak of the Israeli-Lebanese and Palestinian conflicts. It was shown at Aspect Ratio Gallery, Chicago, in 2013.

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
summary: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song (2025) is an outdoor sound installation on the Lawn Square of the Aichi Prefectural Ceramic Museum in Seto, commissioned for the performing arts programme of Aichi Triennale 2025. Visitors walk the lawn wearing headphones; with high-resolution GPS and three-dimensional audio, the sounds change with the visitor's movement. The material includes folk songs and life songs improvised by local women, voices and interviews from Seto, and sounds of clay, water, fire and vegetation, with surrounding background sound that the artist says was interpreted by AI.

title: Species series
summary: Species series is a project of autonomous robots conceived as new species that are born, live and die in the city, built from mass-produced everyday objects and waste combined with electronics and mechanics. The robots are released into urban spaces, where - as the Japan Media Arts Festival jury describes - they are run over by cars, stepped on or knocked from their moorings, and the project records their histories. It was shown as an installation of mixed media and video at the Sullivan Galleries, Chicago, in 2012 and at SIGGRAPH Asia 2012, and received the New Face Award in the 16th Japan Media Arts Festival Art Division.

title: Sports Time Machine
summary: Sports Time Machine is a running lane in which people race against past running records projected onto the wall beside them - their own, those of family and friends, or animals whose runs were recorded at a local zoo - while each new run is saved as 3D data that players can manage on personal web pages. It was premiered in a vacant shop on a shopping street in Yamaguchi as part of YCAM's tenth-anniversary programme LIFE by MEDIA, running from 6 July to 1 December 2013, and was built with local citizens, engineers and sponsors. It received an Excellence Award in the Entertainment Division of the 17th Japan Media Arts Festival.

title: Spray and Pray
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: Spray and Pray is a 15-minute speculative animated documentary in Bulgarian about 'mushroom websites', automatically generated news sites that earn advertising revenue by spreading disinformation. Its CGI characters are built from anonymised research data and performed roles and speak with synthetic voices; a mushroom figure speaks only in headlines collected from such sites, which were also analysed with Bulgarian-language machine-learning models. It premiered at Visions du Réel in 2026 and is shown in the Bulgarian Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale.

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
summary: A dome-shaped enclosure built from some 60–70 recycled speaker boxes facing inward, large enough for about half a dozen people. Visitors go inside, take one of four microphones hanging from the ceiling and speak or sing; their voices pass through effects (delay, phaser) and come back out of the speaker walls, so that strangers inside end up making sound together. First built for a performance at Centre des arts actuels Skol (Elektra festival, Montreal) in 2009, it toured festivals in Europe and Canada and became the first acquisition of HEK (Haus der Elektronischen Künste) Basel's media art collection; in 2021 the artist retitled it SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME and stopped using the word "igloo".

title: Stained
summary: A CGI short film set in Mojo, a fictional future in which Black culture transforms American landscapes. It follows Demetrius, a tea master in the Crimson Needles gang, which uses colored flora to mark territory, as he relives being reprimanded for his fascination with a forbidden blue plant. Credits list music by Nathan Buttel and Jeremy Kamal and AI creative direction by Case Miller; it received a Prix Ars Electronica 2024 Award of Distinction in New Animation Art.

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
summary: A grid of archival prints on canvas (54 x 54 inches) made with AI models trained on a dataset of European floral still-life paintings. The central image comes from a model trained slowly on whole paintings; the surrounding images come from a model trained quickly on randomly cropped details of the same paintings. It was shown in custom frames in Agrawal's solo exhibition EXO-stential: AI Musings on the Posthuman at Emami Art, Kolkata, in September 2021; a related video work is titled (Un)Still Life.

title: Stories from the Earth
summary: A video work commissioned for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, shown in a film booth that is introduced by a painted mural at its entrance, with the artist's own narration. The narration retells Greek mythology and African folklore through twin giant brothers whose rivalry splits the earth, and stages the split between Pão de Açúcar in Rio de Janeiro and Morro do Moco in Huambo, Angola.

title: Stranger Visions
media: Material / sculpture | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: For Stranger Visions, Heather Dewey-Hagborg collected hairs, chewed gum and cigarette butts from streets, public bathrooms and waiting rooms in New York City, extracted DNA from them and had selected genetic regions sequenced. From the results she used custom software to computationally generate life-size, full-colour 3D-printed portraits of what the anonymous individuals might look like. Exhibitions show the portraits alongside the collected samples, their collection sites and the inferred traits.

title: Study for Strings
summary: Study for Strings is an eight-channel sound installation made for dOCUMENTA (13) in 2012 and installed at the end of a platform at Kassel Hauptbahnhof. It reworks the 1943 orchestral piece of the same name by Pavel Haas, composed while he was imprisoned in the Theresienstadt concentration camp; Philipsz recorded only the viola and cello parts, so listeners hear those two lines with silences where the other instruments would play. It was later shown at MoMA's Soundings: A Contemporary Score (2013) through eight wall-mounted speakers.

title: Subnormal Europe
summary: A 60-minute music theatre piece commissioned by the City of Munich for the Münchener Biennale and co-produced with the ZKM Hertz-Lab, performed by contralto Noa Frenkel and sound engineer Sebastian Schottke in an installation of three large screens, nine loudspeakers, MIDI-DMX lighting and a wooden cube. Its framing text presents it as an EU-commissioned project in which the performers create live replicas of moments from audiovisual media history, with an interview series published in parallel on Instagram. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Sunshine Monument
media: Online / net art | AI / generative | Screen / monitor
summary: A Whitney artport commission of seven animated black-and-white architectures, one for each weekday, that translate the layout of blocks of text and images on whitney.org into an abstract building populated by wandering figures, centred on a round sun icon and interspersed with text generated by the artist using AI. It first played on the museum website at sunrise and sunset in New York (Sunrise/Sunset series, from July 2023) and from September 2024 ran hourly, opening the On the Hour series.

title: System's Void
summary: System's Void is a sound installation that translates danger signals from Hazardous Gas System (HGS) monitoring at four fracking wells in the United States into sound, accompanied by a video projection of chemical codes used to classify chemicals. At the 2026 Whitney Biennial the sound was amplified through the large pipe in the museum's central staircase; an earlier version, commissioned by the 15th Gwangju Biennale in 2024, was a five-channel sound installation with sand, steel pipes, speakers and amplifiers.

title: Taala Village
summary: Taala Village ('Village of Rhythms') is a pixel-art video game newly commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances). Players move through a virtual island where actions are accompanied by sounds of Sri Lankan instruments such as the thalampata, drums and conch shells, and meet a speculative community that worships fire and practises rituals, legends and folklore, with settings drawn from kovils, Buddhist temples and village habitats.

title: TAFAA – Fertility Device (Uncanny Valley)
summary: TAFAA – Fertility Device (Uncanny Valley) is a sculpture from Chloé Delarue's FERTILITY DEVICE group, part of her ongoing TAFAA (Toward A Fully Automated Appearance) cycle, and is in the collection of HeK (House of Electronic Arts), Basel. Works in the FERTILITY DEVICE group, as documented by her gallery and other collections, combine metal frames, LCD screens showing video, latex, glass, resin and neon or LED light into free-standing or wall-leaning objects that visitors walk around. The specific materials and dimensions of this piece could not be confirmed from a readable source.

title: Tahrir Cinema (Vox Populi)
summary: Tahrir Cinema was a public screening space in Tahrir Square, Cairo, that Lara Baladi co-founded with the Egyptian media collective Mosireen during the summer 2011 sit-in; she describes it as the first project to emerge from Vox Populi, her ongoing archive of the 2011 Egyptian revolution. Films and video clips of the revolution were projected on a makeshift screen at the entrance of the square to an audience seated on the ground, and people could also bring and exchange raw footage on USB flash drives and DVDs.

title: Tales of the Copper Cross Garden: Episode I
summary: A video installation made for documenta 14 (2017) and shown at EMST – National Museum of Contemporary Art, Athens, listed as video, photographs, copper plate, copper crosses and coins. The film (about 43 minutes) shows workers in a present-day copper processing plant in Katanga, DR Congo, turning copper into wire, with a soundtrack of colonial-era church songs by the Congolese choir of the Singers at the Copper Cross and quoted text by the philosopher Valentin-Yves Mudimbe. It is shown with an archival black-and-white photograph of choirboys wearing copper Katanga crosses.

title: TALK SHOW
summary: TALK SHOW is a 27-minute color film with sound, the final part of Jordan Strafer's Loophole trilogy, shown in a dark gallery with armchairs at the Whitney Biennial 2026. It unfolds across two periods: the turn of the millennium, shot in color (including a reenactment of John F. Kennedy Jr.'s last radio exchange before his 1999 plane crash), and the afterlife, shot in black and white. Most of the film is a daytime talk show in which a host questions a panel of men who confess to rapes while the women they raped watch from backstage; the screenplay draws on news footage and self-help media.

title: tele-present water
media: Robotics / kinetics | Network / data | Material / sculpture
summary: tele-present water is a kinetic installation in which a lattice of wooden rods hangs from nylon threads and is moved by seventeen servo motors controlled by a computer. The motors are driven by wave intensity and frequency data from a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration data buoy in the Pacific (station 51003, or station 46246 in the 2011 WRO version), so that visitors see the grid reproduce the movement of water at that distant location. A version driven by wave data recorded on Lake Superior was also made in 2011.

title: Templo da água: rio Tietê
summary: A circular sound installation in which long copper flutes connected to glass bulbs are suspended and moved by a mechanical system that dips them into a basin of water; the filling and emptying of the bulbs pushes air through the tubes and makes them sound. The water was collected from the upper Tietê River, is kept oxygenated during the show and was to be returned to the river afterwards. Visitors sit on benches arranged around the basin and listen; at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo the work was also activated by performances by Vásquez and Esmeralda Ramírez (Werebere group).

title: Temporary Stored
summary: A sound work built from recordings in the Sound Archive of the Royal Museum for Central Africa (Tervuren), field recordings and synthesizers, presented as shorter fixed-media pieces and a longform radiophonic piece. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023 and was exhibited at the Ars Electronica Festival 2023; it also received an Honorary Mention at the 2023 Prix Palma Ars Acustica.

title: Terminus
media: VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture | Sound
summary: Terminus is a virtual reality work in five parts built from drawings by Jess Johnson, animated by Simon Ward with developer Kenny Smith and soundtracks by Andrew Clarke. Commissioned by the National Gallery of Australia and The Balnaves Foundation, it opened at the NGA in May 2018, where each part was housed in its own architectural structure on a full-scale tessellated floor map. Wearing a headset, the visitor passes through five realms (Fleshold Crossing, Known Unknown, Scumm Engine, Gog & Magog, Tumblewych), selecting each by looking at a portal, with no hand controllers.

title: Thank you for your souvenir, UK!
summary: A three-minute animated short film about a Chinese international student's year of study in the UK, in which identical closed-eyed ragdoll figures are pushed through the system. It received an Honorary Mention in the New Animation Art category of Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: The 3rd I
media: Camera / computer vision | Performance / body | Online / net art
summary: The 3rd I (3rdi) is a camera surgically mounted on the back of Wafaa Bilal's head that, from 15 December 2010 and for a planned year, took an image automatically once a minute and sent it via a laptop carried on his body and a 3G connection to the website 3rdi.me. Commissioned by Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art, Doha, for the exhibition Told/Untold/Retold, it was also shown there as a three-room installation in which banks of screens display the images and respond to the number and movement of visitors.

title: The Anatomy Lessons
summary: A single-channel video by Rashid Rana, dated 2011–2013, shown at Aspinwall House, Fort Kochi, as part of the Kochi-Muziris Biennale. The biennale's Google Arts & Culture entry places it in a body of work in which Rana addresses divides between East and West, static and movement, and formal and conceptual. Project support is credited to Chatterjee & Lal and Chemould Prescott Road, Mumbai.

title: The Buddhist Bug, Into the Night
summary: The Buddhist Bug, Into the Night is a two-channel video projection (9:48 minutes, colour, sound, looped) commissioned for the 8th Asia Pacific Triennial of Contemporary Art (APT8, QAGOMA, Brisbane, 2015-16), with video by Masahiro Sugano (Studio Revolt). It shows the Buddhist Bug - Ali in a long saffron, caterpillar-like costume whose hood resembles a hijab - in its first night-time appearance, moving through Phnom Penh among motorbikes, food stalls and nightclubs, with frames sped up and slowed down. It belongs to the ongoing Buddhist Bug series of performances, photographs and videos that Ali began in 2012 after returning to Cambodia.

title: The Butcher's Son
summary: A single figurative image generated by a chain of generative adversarial networks (GANs): a randomly generated stick figure is fed to a first GAN that produces a low-resolution painterly image, which further GANs upscale and add detail to. The artist selects one output from thousands of variations. It is shown as a print on paper (giclée/ink on cotton rag); the V&A dates the work 2017 and lists it in Klingemann's Imposture Series, and it received the Lumen Prize Gold Award in 2018.

title: The Character of Characters: An Animation by Xu Bing
summary: The Character of Characters is a five-channel animated video installation of about 17 minutes, commissioned by the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco for the 2012 exhibition Out of Character: Decoding Chinese Calligraphy. Shown as one wide landscape across five projections, it begins with the single stroke of the character for 'one' and moves through calligraphy, painting (including Zhao Mengfu's Lotus Sutra calligraphy and Autumn Colors on the Qiao and Hua Mountains), diagrams and text, touching on the genesis of writing, copying in art and society, and symbols and brand names in contemporary China.

title: The Daladala Verse
summary: An XR project on Tanzania's daladala minibuses, developed in the S+T+ARTS4Africa residency hosted by OnaStories and shown at Ars Electronica 2024. The 2026 version is a 5-minute 360° immersive documentary for Meta Quest in which the viewer rides along with Fatuma, the only female conductor on the Mawasiliano–Masaki route in Dar es Salaam.

title: The East Japan Earthquake Archive
media: Network / data | Online / net art | VR / AR / XR
summary: The East Japan Earthquake Archive is a digital archive on Google Earth that maps photographs, 360-degree panorama images, video testimonies of disaster victims (collected with the Asahi Shimbun and recorded binaurally by student volunteers) and a layer of geotagged tweets from the 24 hours after the earthquake of 11 March 2011. Users browse the material from a bird's-eye view and along a timeline; an iPhone/iPad app, eARthquake 311, shows the data on maps and overlaid on the street through augmented reality. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Communities at the Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: The Echinoidea Future – Adriatic Sensing
media: Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor | Network / data
summary: An installation developed from the Zero Pollution Adriatic residency (UR Institute, STARTS4Water, 2021/2022) on how anthropogenic liquid waste and low oxygen levels affect sea urchin habitats in the southern Adriatic. It combines glassblown sculptures based on laboratory experiments exposing sea urchins to pollutants with experimental setups and synchronised screens showing three decades of Copernicus environmental data (temperature, pH, oxygen, salinity) transformed with AI. It received an Honorary Mention at the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.

title: The End of Eating Everything
summary: The End of eating Everything is Wangechi Mutu's first animated video, about eight minutes long, made with the recording artist Santigold and commissioned by the Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University for the 2013 survey Wangechi Mutu: A Fantastic Journey. Santigold appears as a planet-like creature whose body is covered in human limbs and machine parts; it drifts through a polluted, darkened sky and devours a flock of birds. The soundtrack, also by Mutu, combines industrial and organic sounds.

title: THE END OF HOLOCENE: On Karachi's Islands… For The Record
summary: A work shown at Lahore Biennale 03 drawn from about fifteen years of Qaiser's photographic and film recording in the mangrove forests of Bundal and Khiprianwala Islands, Korangi Creek, Karachi, documenting the forest and its cutting. It builds on more than 200 short films he has made and distributed weekly, with notes, as an open educational resource.

title: The Flower Field
summary: An installation of thousands of small flowers hand-crocheted from human hair – hair of cancer patients, survivors and donors in the Hair for Hope charity programme – arranged on a lightbox made from a repurposed bed frame, under glass sheets and lit by LEDs. It was conceived for the Hair for Hope exhibitions in Bangkok in 2012; The Nation's report on 'Hair for Hope: The New Beginning' at the Ardel Gallery of Modern Art describes 2,000 hair flowers resting in an enclosed light bed. The work is in the Singapore Art Museum collection.

title: The Full Story
summary: The Full Story is a short film (about eight minutes), directed by Daisy Jacobs and co-directed by Christopher Wilder, in which Toby, selling his childhood home, recalls his parents' divorce in the 1970s and 80s. It is animated life-size with painted 2D characters on walls, 3D arms, half-painted half-real sets that turn and morph between rooms, and live actors (pixilation) blended into the painted scenes. It received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2018.

title: The Glamorous Boys of Tang (1985, Chui Kang-Chien)
summary: A four-channel video installation in the form of a folding screen that re-shoots scenes from the script of Chiu Kang-Chien's 1985 film The Glamorous Boys of Tang that were missing from the released film, using performers from a range of gendered bodies and subcultures. It was shown in Taiwan in 2018–19, won the 17th Taishin Visual Arts Award, and also exists as a short film.

title: The Great Indecision Council
summary: The Great Indecision Council is a large-scale outdoor light and sound installation, a circle of light about 25 metres across with 12-channel sound, that translates in real time the most frequently searched terms on Google Search and Google News in the host country into words, visual pulses and computer-generated chants. Visitors step inside the circle while others watch from nearby. It was first produced for the Into The Great Wide Open festival on the island of Vlieland (NL) in September 2018 with MU art space, and received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: The Great Orator
media: VR / AR / XR | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: The Great Orator is a 40-minute nonlinear VR story world by Daniel Ernst (The Shoebox Diorama) about a TV preacher whose consciousness lives on as an AI after her death. The visitor explores spaces such as a preserved house, a mainframe holding her followers' shared consciousness and an infinite parking lot, and points a hand at objects to receive her memories, which are generated from the visitor's interaction, random Internet input and live news feeds and differ on each visit. It premiered at Venice Immersive 2025.

title: The Half
summary: A media installation of 25-letter pixelated typography made from 100 speaker units that play sound waves generated from archived mass-media material. Flour on the speakers makes the sound waves visible, and the letters eventually spell the phrase "Growing Gap Between the Halves". It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2013 and was a Jury Selection in the Art Division of the 17th Japan Media Arts Festival.

title: The Innocence of Unknowing
media: AI / generative | Camera / computer vision | Performance / body
summary: The Innocence of Unknowing is an AI archival project, two-channel essay film and live performance examining U.S. news media coverage of mass shootings since the 1960s, studying footage of people retreating. In the performance the artists question an AI model, trained on humanities texts, about its readings of the archive footage, shown alongside computer-vision analyses such as object and pose detection. It had its world premiere at Tribeca Immersive 2025 ('In Search of Us').

title: The Intelligent Guerilla Beehive
media: Material / sculpture | Sensor / interaction | Network / data
summary: A bio-art installation and research project: a beehive designed for urban environments to shelter swarming bee colonies, whose outer membrane, the 'Sensorial Skin', is a fabric combining organic and electronic elements in which bacteria change colour in response to pollution. It grew out of Maes's Brussels rooftop Bee Laboratory, where observation beehives with monitoring technology produced data on bee behaviour, and her Laboratory for Form and Matter, where she works with propolis, chitin, fungi and bacteria. It was shown at Ars Electronica in 2017, where it received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art.

title: The Laughing Snake
media: Online / net art | Text / print | Material / sculpture
summary: The Laughing Snake is a hypertext narrative on the Whitney Museum's artport, co-commissioned with Liverpool Biennial and FACT for Liverpool Biennial 2018, and part of Allahyari's project She Who Sees The Unknown. It retells a myth from the Kitab al-bulhan (Book of Wonders) about a female snake who terrorises a city and dies laughing when shown her reflection in a mirror; after a narrated introduction the reader clicks hyperlinked passages, some leading to the artist's personal stories of growing up in Iran. An installation version with a 3D-printed sculpture, mirrored panels and a touch screen is in the Whitney collection.

title: The Maw Of
media: Online / net art | VR / AR / XR | Screen / monitor
summary: A web-based animation with an augmented-reality layer, commissioned for the Whitney Museum's artport and co-commissioned by KW Institute for Contemporary Art, Berlin. In the browser, a ghostly female figure drawn in a manga style moves through layers of interfaces, elements of whitney.org, a graph of the nervous system, a web console, parental-guidance alerts and military infrared imagery; scanning an on-screen QR code opens an AR layer on the viewer's phone that adds text and moves the figure out of the browser onto the device. A site-specific version (five-channel video, LED screens, sculpture and a hand-tracking VR environment) was shown 15–18 September 2022 at the Tieranatomisches Theater, Berlin.

title: The Oracle: Ritual for the Future (for humans and non-humans)
summary: The Oracle: Ritual for the Future is a 60-minute immersive performance by Victorine van Alphen (Studio Brave New Human) in which the audience moves through a 360-degree screen environment. Starting from the personal story and archival material of two AI enthusiasts, the audience is first given control and then overtaken by non-human entities and AI-generated images; in one scene, audience members who consented have their image altered by AI. It premiered at IDFA DocLab 2025.

title: The Other Dakar
summary: The Other Dakar is a 360° virtual reality film directed by the Dakar-based designer and artist Selly Raby Kane and produced by Electric South. A young girl receives a message and is guided through a series of encounters with mythological beings in a hidden 'other' Dakar, filmed in locations in the city. It premiered at the Berlinale in 2017 and was shown at the Tribeca Film Festival the same year.

title: The Power Loom
artist: Lesiba Mabitsela, Meghna Singh, Simon Wood
media: AI / generative | VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture
summary: The Power Loom is a multimedia installation that digitally weaves African textiles. It is one part of The Founders Pillars; the other part is a site-specific augmented reality experience that uses the same patterns to wrap the columns of the New York Stock Exchange as a memorial to enslaved peoples. It had its world premiere at Tribeca Immersive 2025 ('In Search of Us', WSA / Water Street Projects, 6–29 June 2025), and the project received a S+T+ARTS Prize Africa Award of Distinction in 2025.

title: The Quiet Weight of Shadows
summary: The Quiet Weight of Shadows is an installation shown at Aspinwall House in the Kochi-Muziris Biennale 2025-26 about the history of the ULFA insurgency in Assam. Visitors walk through a field of red- and green-lit artificial carnivorous plants that emit news broadcasts from the 1990s to 2010 in Assamese, Hindi and English, with watchtowers in which video interviews with former ULFA members play, and a reconstructed burnt house holding real archival newspapers, photographs, pamphlets and documents. The installation also screens the artist's film Whispers Beneath the Ashes (2025).

title: The Red Man
summary: A digital portrait painted in Photoshop and posted online in June 2020: a figure in red hues with uncoloured eyes against a red background. After it circulated widely on social media, the artist sold prints of it and it was later sold as an NFT on SuperRare.

title: The Refusal of Time
summary: The Refusal of Time is a half-hour, five-channel video installation made for dOCUMENTA (13) in Kassel in 2012, developed from conversations between Kentridge and historian of science Peter Galison about the history of the control of time. Films are projected on three walls around a large wooden breathing machine ('the elephant'), with music and voices played through four megaphones; imagery includes metronomes, maps, torn-paper figures and a shadow procession. It was made with filmmaker Catherine Meyburgh, composer Philip Miller and dancer Dada Masilo.

title: The Revolving Internet
summary: The Revolving Internet is a website that shows the Google home page steadily rotating while it remains usable for searching, soundtracked by Dusty Springfield's 'Windmills of your Mind'. Visitors search and browse through the turning page, and could reach other sites through it. It launched in 2010 as part of a series of browser-based works by Dullaart that animate the Google search page; it originally embedded Google in an iframe and now runs through a dedicated proxy built with Jonas Lund.

title: The Rift
summary: The Rift is a 6-minute 360° fulldome dance film shot in Zimbabwe, in which four dancers perform a shared choreography across forests, plains, urban settings and abandoned or painted buildings, with water as the unifying element. It premiered at IDFA DocLab in November 2025, shown in the ARTIS-Planetarium dome in Amsterdam and in a smaller dome in the DocLab Exhibition. It was made by 4Pi Productions (Wales) with Matamba Film Labs and AfriKera Arts Trust (Harare) through the XR Labs collaboration.

title: The River is a Circle
media: Screen / monitor | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: A software-driven generative animation made with James Schmitz and Blake Goble and shown on a large video wall on the Whitney Museum's fifth-floor terrace (Hyundai Terrace Commission, April 2025 – January 2026). It shows the Hudson River split between life above and below the water and changes by algorithmic probability with real-time weather, season, tides and marine traffic. The terrace also holds oyster reef balls and marine debris, and a special edit ran nightly on Times Square billboards in September 2025 as a Midnight Moment.

title: The Silence (Two Suns)
summary: An installation at Aichi Triennale 2025 in a former greengrocer's shop in a Seto shopping arcade, with a display window covered in mirrors. Visitors enter through an automatic door into a room where the floor is covered with Suna Kira (tailings from refining silica sand mined in Seto). Unfired flowers made of Seto clay lie on it and fall into the sand over time. Paintings, video and lighting that turns on and off are also used.

title: The Sonic Waraca
summary: The Sonic Waraca is a textile controller based on the waraca, an Andean sling, made for the Textile Museum of Canada's Gathering project with the curatorial collective Mending the Museum, in response to Peruvian textiles in the museum's collection. It works as part of a quadraphonic sound system: its position shifts sound among the speakers and modifies recorded sounds from protests in Peru. Online it is presented as an audio piece.

title: The Teaching Tree
summary: The Teaching Tree is a 40-metre-long sculptural installation of palm fronds painted black on a metal structure, animated internally by pneumatics, made for the National Pavilion of Saudi Arabia at the 59th Venice Biennale (Arsenale, Sale d'Armi, 23 April–27 November 2022), curated by Reem Fadda. The form starts as a thin point and widens along the length of the pavilion towards the entrance; visitors walk beside it as it rises and falls as if breathing, with the scent of dried palm leaves in the room.

title: The Thinking Ocean
media: Online / net art | AI / generative | Sound
summary: The Thinking Ocean is an online interactive generative work commissioned by the Whitney Museum for its artport website, part of the artists' series Cosmosapience. Viewers move through a simulated underwater scene of particles and bubbles that turns into patterns resembling cells, circuitry and code, driven by motion-captured choreography, with a 20-minute audio loop of spoken-word poetry; touching the screen moves the view, and the webcam can bring the viewer's surroundings into the image. It runs in the browser (threejs, WebGPU), every open instance shares a synchronised palette and atmosphere, and it is also shown as an installation and a live performance.

title: The Three Disappearances of Soad Hosni
summary: The Three Disappearances of Soad Hosni is a 70-minute film by Rania Stephan composed entirely of VHS footage from films starring the Egyptian actress Soad Hosni, edited from pirated videotapes. Using no production stills, interviews or information beyond Hosni's performances, it rearranges scenes from her films into a fiction in three parts about her life, opening with Hosni on an analyst's couch. It premiered in competition at the Sharjah Biennial in March 2011.

title: The Treachery of Sanctuary
media: Projection | Camera / computer vision | Sensor / interaction
summary: The Treachery of Sanctuary is an interactive triptych of three 30-foot-high white panels hung from the ceiling behind a shallow reflecting pool. Hidden Kinect cameras capture visitors' shadows and project them onto the panels. In the first panel the shadow dissolves into birds that fly up to join a flock. In the second, birds swoop down and tear pieces off it. In the third, the shadow grows large wings that follow the visitor's arm movements. It opened at The Creators Project at Fort Mason, San Francisco, in 2012 and then toured.

title: The Visitors
summary: The Visitors is a nine-channel video installation with sound, 64 minutes long, in which musicians, each filmed alone in a different room of the 43-room Rokeby mansion in upstate New York, play together a song by Kjartansson and Davíð Þór Jónsson with lyrics by Ásdís Sif Gunnarsdóttir. Visitors walk among the nine screens; residents of the house appear on the terrace, and the performers finally leave the house together. It was commissioned by the Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst, Zurich, and named after ABBA's final album.

title: The Woolworths Choir of 1979
summary: The Woolworths Choir of 1979 is a single-channel HD video installation of about 20 minutes in three episodes. The first uses archival photographs and art-historical captions to describe the choir of a Gothic church; the second edits internet-streamed recordings of singers and dancers into a single choreography of hand gestures; the third assembles news footage, witness statements, inquest testimony and reconstructions of the fatal 1979 fire at the Woolworths store in Manchester. A recurring twisting-wrist gesture and finger clicks link the parts; it was shown in the 2012 Turner Prize exhibition at Tate Britain, for which Price won the prize.

title: The Zone
summary: The Zone is an installation by Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme consisting of a built structure, two-channel video and four-channel sound, with 4–8 minute video and sound clips on 15 LCD screens. Visitors move through its narrow corridors and a room; the project's research documents advertisements, new commercial and residential developments, old political posters and tunnels and walls in the West Bank. It is part of an ongoing research project that also includes photographic series (Desire and Disaster, The Tunnel Series), an online platform and a publication, and was shown at the New Art Exchange and the 5th Jerusalem Show.

title: There Goes Nikki
artist: Idris Brewster, Michele Stephenson, Joe Brewster
media: VR / AR / XR | Material / sculpture | Sound
summary: There Goes Nikki is a five-minute augmented-reality memorial to the poet Nikki Giovanni, in which a volumetric capture of Giovanni recites her poem 'Quilting the Black-eyed Pea (We're going to Mars)' against a cosmic backdrop. At Tribeca Immersive 2025 visitors walked through a living garden installation to a pedestal that anchored the AR experience, with videos before and after it. It was made with Kinfolk Tech and Rada Collaborative.

title: There is the sun
summary: There is the sun is an installation of three motorized mirrors placed on the lawn in front of block 1 of Sint-Maartensdal, a 1960s residential complex in Leuven, Belgium, whose north-south orientation leaves many apartments without direct sunlight. Through a website, residents entered their house number and booked a date and time, and a mirror turned to reflect sunlight through their window. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

title: They Who Saw Nothing but Beauty
summary: They Who Saw Nothing but Beauty is a series of seven jacquard-woven wool tapestries made during the artist's residency at the Jan van Eyck Academie and woven at the TextielLab of the TextielMuseum Tilburg. The compositions are drawn as pixel art in the software Aseprite and show scenes connected to the Battle of Karbala, including a two-faced figure based on Sayyida Zaynab, in dense black-and-white patterns drawn from southern Iraqi carpet-making and Shia iconography. The title refers to Zaynab's reply 'I saw nothing but beauty'; the work received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Tinieblas
summary: Tinieblas (Darkness) is a video installation recording an action in which 13 musicians, placed at 13 spots marking the territorial limits of a town in southern Mexico that is in constant conflict over its borders, play a funeral procession tune known as Tinieblas. It belongs to the artist's investigation of the boundaries of his birthplace, Ocotlán de Morelos, Oaxaca, where boundary markers (mojones) fix the limits between municipalities. It was shown at MUAC, Mexico City, in 2012 in the Sexta Sur programme, co-produced with Museo Amparo, Puebla.

title: TOMORI
summary: A 20-minute mixed reality installation in which the visitor, seated on a physical chair in a small room, takes the place of Shizuku, a young worker undergoing hypnosis with the therapist Ayano, and looks through virtual windows and gaps in the room into scenes of a teenage family life and Tomori's past. The room's windows and crevices require visitors to change position and posture to follow the story. Made as a master's thesis project at Tokyo University of the Arts (GEIDAI GAMES 07, March 2026), it was selected for the Venice Immersive competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival (2026).

title: Toposcan / Baden-Württemberg
summary: A computer-based video installation on eight horizontally aligned 16:9 flat screens driven by eight Mac mini computers, with two loudspeakers. A one-monitor-wide "window" of 360-degree panning landscape footage travels slowly left to right and back across the row; as it advances, the single-pixel edge at its front is stretched into horizontal colour bands, and on the way back the trailing edge leaves pixel-wide vertical freeze-frame stripes that build up a still panorama. It is a version of Takatani's Toposcan series (Ireland 2013, Morocco 2014, Tokyo 2020), developed with ZKM | Karlsruhe for the exhibition "New Sensorium. Exiting from Failures of Modernization" (GLOBALE, 2016) and held in the ZKM collection.

title: Toy Prototype
media: Robotics / kinetics | Screen / monitor | Performance / body
summary: Toy Prototype is an installation of DIY robotic sculptures built by the artist from materials including aluminium profiles and DC motors, operated with remote controllers made of medical simulators and joysticks. The robots are shown alongside videos documenting Jeong's own interactions with the machines and their production process. It was commissioned by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea in 2021 and shown with 9 added videos at the 59th Venice Biennale in 2022.

title: TRANSCLANDESTINA 3020
media: Performance / body | Material / sculpture | Screen / monitor
summary: A multidisciplinary work commissioned for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, made with collaborators from fashion, music and film: a clothing line made from transformed and repurposed worker's uniforms, a fashion show at the Bienal's opening, a sculptural installation of the garments, and a film documenting the creative process. In the installation, visitors meet garments on wooden structures and scaffolding, Polaroid and digital photographs of trans people, and a TV showing the film.

title: Transition sequence for a dream or fight
summary: Transition sequence for a dream or fight is a silent stop-frame animation made from acid-etched copper plates, which borrows the cloud-like scene-change formations used in historical animated productions. It was commissioned by CIRCUIT Artist Moving Image for the group exhibition Leap to the Place of Two Pools, curated by Erin Robideaux Gleeson, at Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery, Wellington (1 February – 6 April 2025).

title: Transits
summary: Transits is a generative video work, about one hour long, made from 24 hours of footage of Aeschenplatz, Basel's busiest traffic junction, where cars, trams and pedestrians pass. Software written by Martin Schneider processes the footage with an artificial neural network in which every pixel corresponds to one neuron, sorting movement patterns and colour schemes into overlapping image layers in which still elements of the square and moving passers-by appear; the video runs from night through dawn and noon to dusk. It was produced for the exhibition Sensing Place at HeK (House of Electronic Arts Basel) in 2012 and is in the HeK collection.

title: Transmission Loss
summary: Transmission Loss is a vibration-based sound sculpture and installation of variable size by Magdi Mostafa, first shown in GLOBALE: New Sensorium at ZKM Karlsruhe in 2016, extending his earlier work Sound Cells (Analog frequencies) (Cairo, 2009) built from hand-made circuits and simple vintage sound devices. Visitors turn the dials of tone generators and handle vibrating devices on a table, altering a field of noise and the feedback between devices. It was also shown at Dak'Art, the Dakar Biennale, in 2018.

title: TRAY TRAY KO
summary: A six-minute HD video performance in which the artist, wearing or pulling a long electric-blue fabric, moves through a forest towards a river and enters it, dragging the soaked fabric upstream until disappearing beneath a waterfall. The title refers to the trayenko (waterfall) in Mapuche cosmology, linked to lawen, medicinal herbs that grow near water; the video ends with a poem in Mapuzungun and Spanish. It was shown at the 2024 Whitney Biennial and is in the collection of the Block Museum, Northwestern University.

title: TROPICS
media: Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision | Sound
summary: TROPICS is a black-and-white animated film about a farm in the Jicaltepec area of Veracruz, Mexico, settled by French farmers in the 19th century; Lavenne made it from point clouds captured with a FARO 3D laser scanner during a months-long residency at the Casa Proal foundation, with the FabLab team of Anáhuac Norte University. The viewer moves through scanned landscapes and scanned local people while recorded voices tell their stories and memories. It won the 2018 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica for Computer Animation.

title: Twin Quasar
media: VR / AR / XR | Online / net art
summary: Twin Quasar is a three-dimensional virtual artwork and space in the Whitney Museum Virtual Landscape, commissioned for the Whitney's artport. It turns two works from the Whitney's collection, László Moholy-Nagy's Space Modulator (1938–40) and Rosalind Bengelsdorf Browne's Compotier II (1938), into navigable 3D models whose forms protrude from the virtual canvas as visitors approach, in an experience that replicates gravitational lensing. It can be visited on the multi-user MONA platform, where visitors see and can talk to each other, and in the Apple Vision Pro.

title: Um Al Dhabab (Mother of Fog)
summary: A two-channel video (29 minutes 45 seconds) shot across locations in Ras Al Khaimah and shown at Sharjah Biennial 15 in the Khorfakkan Art Centre. Through the perspectives of the ghost of an Al Qasimi pirate and a British naval officer, the film recounts the 1819 siege of Al Dhayah fort and the subsequent treaty, using TikTok-style graphics and internet aesthetics. Visitors watch from floral-patterned bean bags.

title: Unknown Label
media: Screen / monitor | Camera / computer vision | Network / data
summary: Unknown Label is a single- or multi-channel video installation of about 16 minutes about online micro-workers in Venezuela, Kenya and the Philippines who outline and label images ("image segmentation") used to train self-driving cars for German and US car manufacturers. It combines the workers' testimonies with images they passed on and an animated digital collage of annotated images and a 3D map of the world as seen by self-driving cars, moving from single-colour segmentation to a city-scale 3D data visualisation. It was developed in 2023 during a European Media Art Platform residency at Werkleitz, received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2024, and was later released for cinema as Their Eyes (2025, with Lucas Azémar).

title: Unsubtitled
summary: A video and sound installation first shown at NhaSan Studio, Hanoi, in 2010: ten projectors loop life-size figures onto 19 wooden cut-out screens in a darkened room. The figures are artists from the Nha San Studio community, each of whom faces the camera, eats an item of food and then states their name and the name of the food. Exhibition texts place it after a directive by the cultural police to pause exhibitions at Nha San Studio following photographs of a nude performance by artist La Thi Dieu Ha; it was later shown at the Singapore Biennale 2013.

title: Us Dead Talk Love
summary: Us Dead Talk Love is a 37-minute two-channel video with surround sound, commissioned by and first shown at Chisenhale Gallery, London (21 September - 11 November 2012), alongside a suite of painted and collaged panels. A computer-generated bald head mapped with the artist's own features speaks a monologue that starts from finding an eyelash under the foreskin; the artist described the premise as two cadavers in dialogue about their lives, decay and love, interrupted by a chorus.

title: Ventilated Pipe Progenies In Another Elsewhere
summary: A site-specific installation for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo (2025), adapted from Buhlungu's 2024 project long time lung time continuuum!!! (a conver-something) at KIT - Kunst im Tunnel, Düsseldorf. A group of metal ventilation pipes extends from the ceiling of the Pavilion and descends beneath it, connected to the building's ventilation system; the pipes move air in loops and produce whistling, huffing and tonal sounds, exchanging air circulated by visitors.

title: Versión libre
summary: Versión libre is a multichannel video and sound installation (five simultaneous projections, 5.1 sound and five large-format photographs) made with demobilised members of Colombia's armed conflict, first shown at the VI Premio Luis Caballero at Galería Santa Fe, Bogotá, in 2011. A large central screen carries the testimony of balaclava-wearing ex-combatants, whose voices spread through the room as echo and murmur, while three narrow, larger-than-life projections show bodies walking back and forth and another video shows people walking away with their backs turned.

title: VFRAME: Visual Forensics and Metadata Extraction
media: Camera / computer vision | AI / generative | Network / data
summary: VFRAME (Visual Forensics and Metadata Extraction) is a research project and open-source computer-vision toolkit by Adam Harvey for human rights researchers and investigative journalists who work with large archives of conflict-zone video. It began in 2017 as a prototype using object detection to locate illegal munitions in footage of the Syrian conflict, was developed with the Syrian Archive and Mnemonic.org into a visual search engine for million-scale video datasets, and from 2019 used 3D-modelled synthetic training images, for example of the AO-2.5RT cluster munition, to train detectors for objects with few real examples. It received an Award of Distinction in Artificial Intelligence & Life Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: Vigil
summary: Vigil is a two-minute digital video with sound, made for Moffatt's exhibition My Horizon in the Australian Pavilion at the 2017 Venice Biennale. It intercuts news images of asylum-seeker boats, including coverage of the December 2010 boat wreck off Christmas Island, with close-ups from Hollywood films of actors such as Elizabeth Taylor, Julie Christie and Donald Sutherland looking through windows or binoculars, so that they appear to watch the disaster; the refugees' bodies are blocked out with colour and the sea is tinted red. It is shown as a looped screen work and is held by QAGOMA and M+, Hong Kong.

title: Visualizing Palestine
media: Network / data | Text / print | Online / net art
summary: Visualizing Palestine is a project, initiated by Ramzi Jaber and co-founded with Joumana al Jabri, that turns research and data on Palestinian experiences into infographics, published first on its website and republished online, in print and in several languages. Its first infographic, Hunger Strikes (February 2012), set out the physical effects of a hunger strike alongside a history of hunger strikes as a tool of non-violent struggle, at the time of Khader Adnan's hunger strike. It received a Distinction in the Prix Ars Electronica Digital Communities category in 2013.

title: Voices of Aliveness
summary: Voices of Aliveness invites participants to ride bicycles equipped with a GPS recorder and a video camera along a 'shouting circuit' at La Martinière near Nantes, France, and to shout as loud as they can during the ride. Each ride is recorded and put online as a ring-shaped trace of path and voice, and the rings are compiled into a tower-like 'time tunnel'; the composer Yasuaki Shimizu arranged the recorded voices for the soundtrack. Produced in 2012 by the École supérieure des beaux-arts de Nantes Métropole within Estuaire, it received an award in Interactive Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: VOID
summary: VOID (2022-ongoing) is a touring performance in which Joshua Serafin embodies a nonbinary deity, drawing on myths of the creation of the Philippine archipelago; it is part of the series Cosmological Gangbang. At the 60th Venice Biennale (2024, Nucleo Contemporaneo, Arsenale) audiences in a dark room watched Serafin move around a central crater in the floor while covering their body in a black, viscous substance, with light and smoke, video and sound; spectators were given ponchos.

title: Void in Resonance
summary: Void in Resonance is a multi-channel film installation about El Campo Pesquero de Playa Bagdad, a community at the eastern end of the Mexico–U.S. border, four kilometres from SpaceX's spaceport in Boca Chica, Texas. It shows a SpaceX launch through the perspectives of people working in the oyster field, juxtaposing Playa Bagdad's vernacular architecture with elements evoking SpaceX designs in deliberately underexposed images. It was produced through the 2025 CIFO x Ars Electronica Award and premiered at Ars Electronica Festival 2025 (POSTCITY, Linz).

title: Wa akhiran musiba
summary: Wa akhiran musiba (At Last, a Tragedy) is a 15'49" video written, directed, shot and produced by Maya Shurbaji (editing Ayman Nahle, sound design Ziad Moukarzel). It opens with a WhatsApp exchange in Arabic between the artist and a friend, Louay, about life and death, followed by a man's voice describing sleep-deprivation torture in prison; through family footage and childhood images the non-linear narrative connects the imprisonment of the artist's father with her own history, including her gender transition, using archive material for Damascus and the past and footage from Beirut for the present. It premiered at the 68th Berlin Film Festival in 2018 and was shown at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019-2020).

title: Walled Unwalled
summary: Walled Unwalled is a 20-minute single-channel video installation in which Lawrence Abu Hamdan, filmed behind the windows of recording booths in the Funkhaus studios in former East Berlin (the GDR state radio headquarters), delivers a monologue on legal cases in which evidence was heard or experienced through walls, doors or floors. These include the US thermal-imaging case Kyllo v. United States, the Oscar Pistorius murder trial and testimonies of survivors of Saydnaya prison in Syria, with projected images, moving walls and sound. At Tate Modern's Tanks (2018) the video was projected onto a wall of semi-transparent panels that visitors first saw from behind.

title: Wantee
summary: Wantee is a film installation, commissioned by Tate and Grizedale Arts for the exhibition Schwitters in Britain at Tate Britain in 2013, in which a film tells a fictional story of Prouvost's grandfather, a conceptual artist and friend of Kurt Schwitters, who disappeared while digging a tunnel from his home towards Africa. Visitors watch the film in a room furnished like a tea party, with objects including some made by potters and community groups; the title is the nickname of Schwitters's partner Edith Thomas, from her habit of asking 'want tea?'. Shown again at the Turner Prize exhibition in Derry-Londonderry, where tea and cakes were served, it won the 2013 Turner Prize.

title: Washed Out "The Hardest Part"
summary: An official music video for the Washed Out song "The Hardest Part", made with OpenAI's text-to-video model Sora: a continuous forward push through time following a couple from school through marriage and later life across several decades. Trillo generated around 700 clips and edited about 55 of them into the roughly four-minute video; it received the 2024 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica (AI in Art) and was shown in the Ars Electronica Festival exhibition.

title: Wastelands
summary: Wastelands is a biological art project that speculates on a future 500 years from now in which humans fuel the world with biogas made from their own waste. It consists of small biogas generator sculptures in glass and bioplastic housing methanogenic bacteria, archaea and bacteriophages, developed with anaerobic-digestion researchers at Michigan State University. It was shown at the Broad Art Museum, MSU (2018-2019).

title: We Are All Made of Light
summary: An immersive installation of projectors, spatial sound, AI recognition software and over 63,000 reflective woven threads, first shown at MadArt Studio, Seattle (6 Oct – 1 Dec 2018). The system detects visitors' bodies, records their silhouettes and projects them back into the space as star-like light trails, which remain after they leave and accumulate with the trails of earlier visitors. The technical system was developed with Microsoft researcher Mihai Jalobeanu; it received the Lumen Prize 3D/Interactive Award in 2019.

title: We Are Dead Animals
media: VR / AR / XR | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: We Are Dead Animals is a VR game, premiered at IDFA DocLab 2025, built from 3D scans (photograms) of dead animals the artist found in his surroundings, placed in a landscape that is his interpretation of paradise. Players fly through it with hand-tracking, revive animals, read about how they died, collect them, combine their body parts into new creatures, release them or eat them to extend a limited lifespan. At IDFA it was installed inside a nest built of organic material.

title: Wellenwald mit Bunker
summary: Wellenwald mit Bunker is an installation of a spruce trunk covered in aluminium foil, leaning on a concrete object shaped like a bunker; antennae mounted on the trunk are wired into the concrete object. Inside, a speaker plays a composed drone sound file together with signals the antennae pick up from electromagnetic waves of nearby devices such as mobile phones, so visitors' devices alter the sound in real time. It is a reinterpretation of Joseph Beuys's 1972 work Fichtenstamm mit Munitionskiste (Munitionskiste mit Fichtenstamm).

title: what colours can we dream in this night filled with salt?
summary: A film installation by Julianknxx first shown at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo (6 September 2025 – 11 January 2026) and later in the Bienal's traveling exhibitions in Goiânia, Curitiba and Santiago. Visitors enter a dark room with white walls where a black-and-white video is shown.

title: Where Do the Ants Go?
media: Sensor / interaction | Screen / monitor | Material / sculpture
summary: A multiplayer video game installation inside a large walk-in sculpture of an anthill, designed with architect Jeremy Waterfield, in which visitors together steer a digital colony of programmed ants on screens around the interior. Players feed the colony with thoughts they type into the system, and depending on which thoughts are taken up the colony can burn, drown or starve; there is nothing to win or lose. It was first shown at Dhaka Art Summit 2023 and then travelled (Horst Arts and Music Festival, Zeppelin Museum, Pivô São Paulo), with the anthill rebuilt in local materials at each site.

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
media: Online / net art | Sensor / interaction | Material / sculpture
summary: A decision-making web game and NFT project, also presented as an installation with an interactive fibreglass sculpture with LED lights and water fountains, controlled by iPad. Players move through a labyrinth of metaphorical decisions (the path of the Divine Mother, Human God or Moral High Horse), collect 'wisdom tokens' as free downloadable artworks with a 'moral contract', and can see other online players on a map. Iterations were shown at HEK / Transfer Gallery, the Thailand Biennale 2021, Gray Area Festival 2021 and SeMA Bunker, Seoul; it received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)
media: Material / sculpture | Robotics / kinetics | Screen / monitor
summary: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth was Brazil's presentation at the 59th Venice Biennale (2022), curated by Jacopo Crivelli Visconti. Built on an index of more than 200 Brazilian idiomatic expressions that name body parts, it combines sculptures, photographs and a video; visitors enter through an outsized ear and leave through another, and at intervals a large fabric heart drops from a mouth in the ceiling and inflates to fill the second room. The expressions are captioned in Portuguese, English and Italian.

title: Without Us
summary: Without Us is a project by composer and percussionist Daniel Brandt made up of an album (Erased Tapes, March 2025), a 20-minute short film of the same name directed with Anthony Dickenson and shot in Athens in 2023, and a live performance in which the concert is interwoven with the film. The film follows Gaia, an Uber driver who decides humanity is the world's problem; the album uses field recordings including the hum of Europe's largest mall. The live A/V version premiered at the Barbican in London in April 2025 and was presented at CTM Festival 2026.

title: Written To Not Remain
media: Screen / monitor | VR / AR / XR | Text / print
summary: Written To Not Remain is a 12'30" video work about writing on walls across post-revolution Libya since 2011. It combines archival imagery from a photo archive of over 200 images of wall writings that Barnosa began collecting in 2019 with acts made inside a VR simulation and 3D spatial scans, alongside a text recitation. It is listed among the S+T+ARTS Prize 2025 winners (Ars Electronica).

title: Zoom, Click, Waltz
summary: Zoom, Click, Waltz is a multimedia installation of 13 LED screens, each showing a person or people in a separate apartment window, dancing or not. It began during Singapore's 2020 Covid-19 'Circuit Breaker' lockdown, when the artist mailed letters to neighbours in her building asking them to dance by their living-room windows at a set time; the recordings are stitched together with staged, found and borrowed footage. It was shown at Gillman Barracks, Singapore (21 January - 7 February 2021) and won the 2021 Lumen Prize 3D/Interactive Award.

title: ÑUQA KAUSAKUSAQ QHEPAYKITAPAS / I WILL OUTLIVE YOU
summary: A single-channel HD video with sound (about 15 minutes) using 3-D animation, made after the artist encountered a 1200-year-old Moche ceramic vessel at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin depicting a prisoner about to be sacrificed. In a monologue, the prisoner reflects on the time before his death, his childhood, his transformation into a digital being and his incarceration as an object on museum display and part of an artwork. It was shown in Martínez Garay's solo exhibition I WILL OUTLIVE YOU at GRIMM, New York (2018) and at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019).
